title: The edge of the world
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H60 The edge of the world HD.mp4
description: As the Earth is mapped, knowledge is only a click away, and human adventurousness declines, is the end of the unknown changing what it means to be human? Erling Kagge, Joanna Kavenna, Steven Mithen and Maria Balaska debate.
filename: HTLGI2026_H60 The edge of the world HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning novelist and one of Granta's Best Young British Novelists. Erling Kagge is a Norwegian explorer, philosopher, and writer. He is the first person in history to reach the North Pole, South Pole, and the summit of Mount Everest on foot. Steven Mithen is an archaeologist whose work explores the evolution of human intelligence, creativity, and social behaviour. Maria Balaska is a philosopher whose work explores subjectivity, ethics, and the limits of experience. HOST: Sophie Scott-Brown
subtitle: Are we witnessing the end of the unknown?

title: The hype and limits of AI
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_L26 Hype and Limits of AI_HD.Second Copy.mp4
description: The world is consumed with the power and potential of AI.  Leading tech names like Altman and Musk have claimed it threatens humanity’s future. All while trillions of dollars are being invested.  The extraordinary success of Large Language Models, initiated by the 2017 breakthrough transformer/attention coding principles, is seen as just the beginning.  More data, more computing it is assumed will deliver ever more powerful AI. But a growing number of critics argue these models are in fact unintelligent word calculators that have already reached their peak as human training data has been exhausted. To be intelligent they would have to interact with the world, while language models merely find patterns in human text predicting what comes next and nothing more.
filename: HTLGI2026_L26 Hype and Limits of AI_HD.Second Copy.mp4
speaker_desc: Michael Wooldridge is an Oxford computer scientist and one of the world’s foremost authorities on AI. His book The Road to Conscious Machines argues that the hype around AI distracts us from the more immediate risks that the technology poses. Audrey Borowski is a Leverhulme Early Career Fellow at Cambridge specialising in the philosophy of AI. Her research argues that data and algorithmic systems have become a new form of ideology, undermining democratic politics. Tipped by The Times as "the next Einstein," Sabrina Pasterski is a theoretical physicist specializing in celestial holography. Based at the Perimeter Institute, she founded and leads the Celestial Holography Initiative, aimed at uniting our understanding of spacetime with quantum theory. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist account of the relationship between language and the world. He extends the same principles to artificial intelligence, with radical implications for what machines can and cannot do.
subtitle: Is the latest technology our friend or foe?

title: The dangerous urge to punish
description: Most of us see punishment as a necessity, even as a moral good needed to prevent bad actors in society and rehabilitate wrongdoers. But what if the urge to punish has darker, more sinister roots?
filename: HTLGI2026_L57 The Dangerous Urge to Punish.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Andy West is the author of The Life Inside and the Executive Producer of the acclaimed BBC adaptation of that book Waiting for the Out.
subtitle: Waiting For the Out

title: The institutions that failed Gaza

description: Norman Finkelstein and Roger Hearing discuss the failure of international institutions to prevent the destruction of Gaza.

speaker_desc: Norman Finkelstein is one of the most high-profile controversial political scientists writing today. He has spent decades as a leading critic of Israeli policy. His 2025 book, Gaza’s Gravediggers, turns his scrutiny on the institutions he accuses of complicity in Gaza’s destruction.
subtitle: Reckoning with descruction

title: Why we should embrace cybersex, with Trudy Barber
description: Artist and futurologist Trudy Barber argues that the advent of cybersex is forcing us to reimagine the boundaries between the human and the robotic.
speaker_desc: Dr. Trudy Barber is a fine artist, sexual futurologist, and pioneer of cybersex research who created one of the first virtual reality sex environments in the early 1990s. Her work focuses on the intersection of human desire and technology, spanning virtual reality, AI, sex robotics, and the posthuman future of intimacy.

title: When compassion turns dangerous
description: Join Kathleen Stock in debate with Mary Ann Sieghart on the ethics of assisted dying.
filename: HTLGI2026_H65 When compassion turns dangerous SD.mp4
speaker_desc: Kathleen Stock is a British philosopher and author who rose to prominence as a central figure in debates over sex, gender, and truth—resigning from the University of Sussex in 2021 and entering the public discourse. Author and broadcaster, Mary Ann Sieghart is a former Times columnist whose work focuses on gender equality, political analysis, and public policy.
subtitle: Should we legalise assisted dying?

title: Carlo Rovelli on the impossibility of a theory of everything
description: Theoretical physicist and best-selling author Carlo Rovelli argues that our theories can only describe parts of our multifaceted relationship to the universe, rather than attempt a theory of everything.
speaker_desc: Theoretical physicist Carlo Rovelli is a pioneer of theories like Loop Quantum Gravity, White Holes, and the relational interpretation of quantum mechanics. His books include Seven Brief Lessons on Physics, which has been translated into 41 languages and sold over a million copies, as well as the bestselling Reality Is Not What It Seems (2015) and White Holes (2023). He was named one of the 100 most influential thinkers in the world by Foreign Policy magazine, and is Emeritus Professor at the Centre de Physique Théorique of Marseille, as well as holding positions at the Santa Fe Institute and the Perimeter Institute.
subtitle: Reality is made of relations

title: One giant conflict for mankind
description: Is space a new military battleground? Kishore Mahbubani, Laura Grego, and Adam Frank ask if space exploration can still benefit all humanity, or if the strongest will make the rules.
filename: HTLGI2026_H193 One Giant Conflict for Mankind.SD.REVISED1.mp4
speaker_desc: Adam Frank is an American astrophysicist, writer, and public intellectual who serves as Professor of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Rochester. Kishore Mahbubani is a Singaporean diplomat and scholar, former President of the UN Security Council, and one of Asia's most influential voices on geopolitics and the historic return of Asia to the global centre stage. Laura Grego is an astrophysicist and director of the Global Security Programme at the Union of Concerned Scientists, specialising in space policy and nuclear safety and security. Philip Ball hosts.
subtitle: War and diplomacy on the final frontier

title: Spacetime and the framework of the world
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H19 Spacetime and the framework of the world.Cut 2.HD.mp4
description: Is the idea of spacetime inherently incompatible with quantum mechanics? Quantum physicists Jonathan Oppenheim, Ivette Fuentes, and Avshalom Elitzur debate.
filename: HTLGI2026_H19 Spacetime and the framework of the world.Cut 2.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Avshalom Elitzur is an Israeli physicist and philosopher at the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research whose Elitzur–Vaidman thought experiment reshaped debates on the role of the observer in quantum theory. Jonathan Oppenheim is a Professor of Quantum Theory at UCL, renowned for developing “post-quantum” models in which spacetime remains classical, but interacts consistently with quantum matter. Ivette Fuentes is a Professor of Quantum Physics at the University of Southampton whose work considers fundamental quantum mechanics, quantum optics and their interplay with general relativity. Bjørn Ekeberg hosts.
subtitle: Probing the nature of time

title: The rise and fall of the educated elite
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_L30 The rise and fall of the educated elite HD.mp4
description: Should we conclude that the educated are no longer winning, and that the future will favour the skilled and the self-taught? Daniel Susskind, Michael Gove, and Thangam Debonnaire debate.
filename: HTLGI2026_L30 The rise and fall of the educated elite HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Michael Gove is Editor of The Spectator and served in cabinet across five government departments for more than a decade. Most consequentially as Secretary of State for Education, where he steered through the biggest changes to English schooling in decades. Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour life peer and former MP for Bristol West who served as Shadow Secretary of State for Culture under Keir Starmer. Her work in the Lords spans arts, cultural diplomacy, AI and copyright. Daniel Susskind is a leading economist, Professor of Business at Gresham College, and a member of the UK Government's Expert Panel on AI and the Future of Work. His new book What Should My Children Do explores how AI is changing the future of education. Mary Ann Sieghart is a journalist, author, and public intellectual committed to dismantling the invisible yet powerful bias she calls “the authority gap.”
subtitle: Is there any future for traditional education?

title: There can be no ultimate map of the universe
description: Philosopher Jenann Ismael, whose work is at the leading edge of trying to connect the theories of physics to our conscious experiences of reality, argues that there can be no complete map or model of physical facts.
speaker_desc: A transformative encounter with a German Sufi philosopher in Cairo set Jenann Ismael on her way to becoming the leading philosopher of physics that she is today. Her work confronts the tension between what physics tells us about reality, and how the world actually seems to us in our conscious experience of it. She tries to ground free will in the nature of thermodynamics, and argues that reality is fundamentally unpredictable.
subtitle: Systems cannot describe themselves consistently

title: The future of the tech crisis
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H66 The future of the tech crisis HD.mp4
description: Cory Doctorow, author of Enshittification, makes the case that monopoly and weak regulation have caused the degredation of the internet, arguing that users, not platforms, need to start seting the terms.
filename: HTLGI2026_H66 The future of the tech crisis HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Cory Doctorow is a Canadian-British author and digital rights activist who has served as European Director of the Electronic Frontier Foundation. He is the author of several books including Enshittification.
subtitle: Building the post-American internet

title: Economists don't understand the nature of power, with Ingrid Harvold Kvangraven
description: Ingrid Harvold Kvangraven argues that the discipline of economics fails to understand its dependence on global power structures shaped by imperialism, class, and inequality.
speaker_desc: Ingrid Harvold Kvangraven is a Senior Lecturer in International Development at King’s College London, founder of the blog Developing Economics and a leading thinker in heterodox economics.
subtitle: Why economics is fundamentally political

title: Buddhism and the emptiness of reality
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_H183 Buddhism and the emptiness of reality.HD.mp4
description: Oxford philosopher Jessica Frazier explains the Buddhist metaphysics of emptiness, and its consequences for our understanding of ethics.
filename: HTLGI2025_H183 Buddhism and the emptiness of reality.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Jessica Frazier is a philosopher at the University of Oxford and Founder of the Journal of Hindu Studies whose research translates classical Indian philosophy into terms that engage contemporary debates on metaphysics and ethics.
subtitle: Buddhism vs Hinduism on the true nature of reality

title: Consciousness has evolutionary roots, with Eva Jablonka
description: Biologist Eva Jablonka advances an evolutionary account of origins of consciousness, arguing that sheer level of complexity it requires to develop is beyond the capacity of artificial intelligence, just as it is for plants and fungi.
speaker_desc: Eva Jablonka is an evolutionary theorist and geneticist whose work pushes biology beyond a strictly gene-centred view of life.
subtitle: Why AI isn't conscious and likely never will be

title: Rethinking the global orthodoxy
description: Former President of PEN International John Ralston Saul argues that a global overreliance on borderless institutions has hollowed out local economies, weakened democratic accountability, and fractured civic trust.
speaker_desc: John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and President Emeritus of PEN International. His 16 works, including Voltaire’s Bastards and The Collapse of Globalism, have been translated into 29 languages in 38 countries.
subtitle: How the illusion of globalization empowered elites

title: Why Plato matters now
description: Professor Angie Hobbs argues that Plato's philosophy can help us understand a host of modern problems, including fake news, autocracy, cancel culture and the limits of wealth.
speaker_desc: Angie Hobbs is the chair for the Public Understanding of Philosophy at Sheffield, and a frequent contributor to the BBC’s In Our Time, Night Waves and The Forum. She is the author of Plato and the Hero and is currently working on a new edition of Plato’s Symposium.
subtitle: Ancient answers to modern problems

title: Time's great mystery
description: Is time part of the essential structure of the universe, an object we can measure, or something else entirely? Tim Maudlin, Ivette Fuentes, Wahida Khandker and Hilary Lawson debate.
speaker_desc: Tim Maudlin is a celebrated philosopher of science, renowned for his work on the foundations of physics and metaphysics. He is also an author and professor at New York University. Wahida Khandker is a philosopher and co-chair of the Society for European Philosophy. Her work is at the cutting-edge of the philosophy of process and the philosophy of biology. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything, has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Ivette Fuentes is a physicist at the University of Southampton and Emmy Fellow at the University of Oxford. Her work and previous collaboration with Roger Penrose considers fundamental quantum mechanics, quantum optics and their interplay with general relativity.
subtitle: What does the clock really measure?

title: Globalisation has failed the Left, with Maurice Glasman
description: Maurice Glasman, founder of the Blue Labour movement, argues that the Left needs to reject open borders, globalisation and the rule of capital, and embrace a conservative strand of socialism that champions tradition, community, and civic association.
speaker_desc: Political theorist, Labour life peer, and a member of the House of Lords, Maurice Glasman founded the Blue Labour movement in 2009.
subtitle: What comes after MAGA?

title: Free will is real
description: Leading physicist George Ellis argues that free will can emerge from complex systems, and that scientific accounts of causality have wrongly dismissed it.
filename: HTLGI2026_H251 Free will is real HD.mp4
speaker_desc: George Ellis is a South African cosmologist and philosopher of science renowned for bridging the gap between physics and metaphysics.
subtitle: Why science cannot ignore human agency

title: The return of the grand narrative
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H260 The return of the grand narrative.SD.mp4
description: Rather than replacing the old religious grand narratives, has science just conjured up new versions? Steve Fuller, Michael Shermer, and Shini Somara debate.
filename: HTLGI2026_H260 The return of the grand narrative.SD.mp4
speaker_desc: Steve Fuller is a Professor of Sociology at the University of Warwick and founder of the research programme of social epistemology, best known for his work on the post-truth condition and the politics of knowledge. Michael Shermer is one of the world's most prominent sceptics and defenders of scientific reason. He's the founding publisher of the widely read Sceptic Magazine, and the executive director of the Sceptics Society. Dr. Shini Somara is an award-winning media broadcaster and a highly accomplaished British mechanical engineer specialising in Computational Fluid Dyanmics. Jack Symes hosts.
subtitle: Does science preach the same story it replaced?

title: Quantum measurement influences the past, with Avshalom Elitzur
description: In this interview, theoretical physicist Avshalom Elitzur argues that quantum physics alters our conception of time and causation: a measurement done in the present influences not only the future, but the past.
speaker_desc: Avshalom Elitzur is a theoretical physicist and philosopher at the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research, whose Elitzur–Vaidman thought experiment reshaped debates on the role of the observer in quantum theory.
subtitle: Time and consciousness in quantum physics

title: Education has lost its way
description: Economist Guy Standing argues that the modern education system has been corrupted by market logic, which encourages AI use and erodes student skills. In this talk, he proposes a new democratic alternative.
speaker_desc: Guy Standing is a trailblazing economist and long-standing advocate for Universal Basic Income. He is a Professorial Research Associate at SOAS University of London and co-founder of the Basic Income Earth Network.
subtitle: Reclaiming learning as a public good

title: Beyond the sci-fi myths of AI
description: Philosopher and historian of economic thought Philip Mirowski argues that artificial intelligence is reshaping what counts as legitimate knowledge and fundamentally altering what it means to be a scientist.
speaker_desc: Philip Mirowski is the Carl Koch Professor of Economics and the History and Philosophy of Science at the University of Notre Dame. He is a leading historian and philosopher of economic thought, known for his trenchant critiques of neoliberalism, the commercialisation of science, and the epistemology of economics.
subtitle: How open science is privatising knowledge

title: The end of the great alliance
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H59 The end of the great alliance.HD.mp4
description: As the US-Europe alliance breaks apart, what next for the global balance of power? Michael Ignatieff, Jeremy Corbyn, and Gillian Tett debate.
filename: HTLGI2026_H59 The end of the great alliance.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour party's leader from 2015 to 2020. He is co-founder and interim leader of Your Party. Michael Ignatieff is a writer, historian, and former Leader of Canada's Liberal Party whose books on nationalism and human rights have established him as a central voice in post–Cold War political thought. One of the few leading economists who predicted the 2008 financial crisis, Gillian Tett is a columnist for the Financial Times and author of several books including Fool's Gold . Rana Mitter hosts.
subtitle: What next for the US and Europe?

title: Disloyalty is not betrayal
description: Yasmin Alibhai-Brown argues that we need to reclaim the courage to be disloyal to the political movements, communities, and identities we support rather than retreating behind the rhetoric of solidarity.
filename: HTLGI2026_H111 Disloyalty is not betrayal HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Yasmin Alibhai-Brown writes a weekly opinion column for The i Paper, focusing on British politics, social justice, and cultural issues. She is an award-winning journalist and was named Broadsheet Commentator of the Year at the Media Freedom Awards. Alibhai-Brown was also the founder of the British Muslims for Secular Democracy.
subtitle: When loyalty becomes complicity

title: The return of Malcolm X
description: Malcolm X is often written off as a slogan or a threat. Join the first Black studies professor in the UK, Kehinde Andrews, as he restores Malcolm X's radical clarity.
filename: HTLGI2026_H47 The return of Malcolm X.SD.mp4
speaker_desc: Kehinde Andrews is the first Black Studies professor in the UK, currently working at Birmingham City University. He is the director of the Centre for Critical Social Research, founder of the Harambee Organisation of Black Unity, and co-chair of the UK Black Studies Association.
subtitle: Recovering the radical philosophy of civil rights

title: The key to the cosmos
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_H170 The key to the cosmos HD.mp4
description: Can mathematics provide an ultimate description of reality? Sarah Hart, Dean Rickles, and Hilary Lawson debate.
filename: HTLGI2025_H170 The key to the cosmos HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Sarah Hart is the first female Professor of Geometry at Gresham College and the author of Once Upon a Prime. Her research focuses on the cutting-edge of group theory. Dean Rickles is historian and philosopher of Modern Physics at the University of Sydney, where he is also a director of the Sydney Centre for Time. He investigates the frontiers of quantum gravity, string theory and the philosophy of the mind. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything, has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Hosted by Jay Shapiro: an award-winning filmmaker, writer, and podcaster.
subtitle: Does mathematics describe reality?

title: The idea of progress is a dangerous lie, with John Gray
description: John Gray argues that the belief in civilizational progress is both false and dangerous—a secular myth that blinds us to the recurring conflicts of history.
speaker_desc: John Gray, hailed as "Britain's best philosopher," is a leading critic of liberalism and the Enlightenment. He has long challenged the belief in inevitable progress, predicting both the 2008 financial crisis and the rise of populism. Jonny Thomson hosts.
subtitle: There is no moral arc of history

title: The science of creativity
description: But Sheila Atim, Olivier Award–winning actor, argues that the divide between art and science is a myth that limits both creativity and scientific innovation
subtitle: Breaking the arts vs science binary

title: New rebels and a failed establishment
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H240 New rebels and a failed establishment HD.mp4
description: Since the French Revolution, the young have rebelled left, but now France, Germany and the US are showing a shift to the far-right in young voters. Should these new rebels be listened to as a challenge to a failed establishment?
filename: HTLGI2026_H240 New rebels and a failed establishment HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords, having served for nine years as MP for Bristol West and as a senior figure in Keir Starmer’s Shadow Cabinet. Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at the University of Buckingham and Director of the Centre for Heterodox Social Science. His research focuses on political demography, national identity, immigration, and cultural change. Louisa Munch is a critical theorist, PhD researcher, and influencer reaching over 200,000 people on social media, translating complex ideas into clear commentary on politics, culture, and power.
subtitle: Should we heed the voice of youth?

title: Science and the unknowable universe
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H247 Science and the unknowable universe HD.mp4
description: Can science ever fully grasp reality? Avshalom Elitzur and Lera Boroditsky explore whether science is a window onto the world — or a refleciton of the mind's limits.
filename: HTLGI2026_H247 Science and the unknowable universe HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Lera Boroditsky is a cognitive scientist and linguist whose research has transformed our understanding of how language shapes thought. Avshalom Elitzur is an Israeli physicist and philosopher at the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research whose Elitzur–Vaidman thought experiment reshaped debates on the role of the observer in quantum theory. HOST: Philip Ball is a British science writer. For over twenty years he has been an editor of the journal Nature for which he continues to write regularly. He now writes a regular column in Chemistry World.
subtitle: How much can science really tell us?

title: What 50 days of silence can teach you, with Erling Kagge
description: Explorer and philosopher Erling Kagge argues one way to find meaning is to deliberately make your life harder. In this interview, he explains the origins of gratitude, talks about his encounter with a polar bear, and explains what he learnt from 50 days of silence in Antarctica.
speaker_desc: Erling Kagge is a Norweigian explorer, philosopher, and writer who has spent his life testing the limits of the physical world and human mind. He is the first person in history to reach the North Pole, South Pole and the summit of Mount Everest on foot. He has also sailed across the Atlantic twice, rounded Cape Horn, and sailed to Antarctica and back. After his record-breaking feat, Kagge founded a publishing house which went on to acquire one of Norway's oldest publishing companies. In 2021, Kagge sold his publishing company and in 2025 he left his position as publisher. His writing on exploration and philosophy has appeared in the Financial Times, The New York Times, and the Guardian.
subtitle: The philosophy of making our life harder

title: Pride and prognosis
description: AI now outperforms clinicians in detecting certain cancers, predicting risks, and spotting patterns no human eye can see. So why are so many doctors resisting it?  Philosopher of medicine Charlotte Blease outlines the costs of clinging to tradition.
speaker_desc: Charlotte Blease is a philosopher of medicine whose research focuses on the ethical, psychological and social dimensions of healthcare innovation, particularly the use of digital and artificial intelligence technologies in clinical settings.
subtitle: Why AI could save care

title: The mystery of the self and the body
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H259 The mystery of the self and the body.HD.mp4
description: Are the self and the physical body fundamentally distinct substances? Join Slavoj Žižek, Monima Chadha, Martine Nida-Rümelin, and Federico Faggin debate the merits and drawbacks of dualism.
filename: HTLGI2026_H259 The mystery of the self and the body.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Slavoj Žižek is a Senior Researcher at the University of Ljubljana and the author of more than fifty books applying Lacanian psychoanalysis and Hegelian philosophy to politics, film, and culture. Monima Chadha is Professor of Indian Philosophy at the University of Oxford. A leading figure in cross-cultural philosophy, her work brings classical Indian traditions into dialogue with contemporary epistemology and the philosophy of mind. Martine Nida-Rümelin is a German philosopher and professor of philosophy at the University of Fribourg in Switzerland. Her work develops and defends what she calls subject-body dualism. Federico Faggin is an Italian-American physicist and engineer who led the design of the world's first commercial microprocessor at Intel in the 1970s, earning him the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.
subtitle: The mind-body problem from East to West

title: Immunity and impunity in a lawless world
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H91 Immunity and impunity in a lawless world HD.mp4
description: Leading international lawyer Philippe Sands argues that combating impunity — the ability of the powerful to escape accountability for atrocities — is more essential now than ever.
filename: HTLGI2026_H91 Immunity and impunity in a lawless world HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Philippe Sands is a writer and lawyer known for his work in international law and human rights. His books chart the use of international law to hold to account violations of international law from Chile's Pinochet to Nazis who fled to avoid the Nuremberg trials. He has emerged as a leading defender of the rule of law around the world in an age where populism and conflict threaten to send the world into anarchy. He is currently a Professor of Laws and the Director of the Centre on International Courts and Tribunals at University College London. He has appeared as a counsel and advocate at the International Court of Justice, the European Court of Justice, the European Court of Human Rights and the International Criminal Court. His most recent book, 38 Londres Street, charts the trial of Pinochet, the first national leader to be tried under international law, and the efforts to hold Nazi officers responsible for the holocaust to account.
subtitle: From Nazis in Patagonia to Pinochet in London

title: Neurodiverse pattern-seeking drives human invention, with Simon Baron-Cohen
description: Simon Baron-Cohen argues that pattern-seeking, or "if-and-then" thinking, fuelled human invention, and is markedly stronger in autistic minds.
speaker_desc: One of Britain’s most influential psychologists, Simon Baron-Cohen is renowned for his pioneering research on autism, empathy, and the cognitive differences between individuals. Professor of Developmental Psychopathology at the University of Cambridge, Baron-Cohen has challenged conventional views of the human mind with a body of work that spans theories of mind, systemizing-empathizing, and the biological basis of social cognition. He is the author of The Essential Difference , Mindblindness , Zero Degrees of Empathy , and The Pattern Seekers , as well as a frequent contributor to the Guardian , Scientific American , and academic journals worldwide. Baron-Cohen’s rigorous research and thought-provoking theories continue to shape contemporary debates on neurodiversity, education, and the nature of human cognition.
subtitle: Rethinking autism and how we approach it

title: Marx, Raymond Williams, and the climate crisis
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H237 Marx, Williams, and the climate crisis.HD better_1.mp4
description: John Merrick explores how Raymond Williams’ Marxist critique of industrial capitalism and its extractive systems are newly relevant in helping to understand and solve the climate crisis.
filename: HTLGI2026_H237 Marx, Williams, and the climate crisis.HD better_1.mp4
subtitle: Ecosocialism's forgotten foundations

title: Warfare in the academy
description: Can education ever be devoid of politics, or should we acknowledge it as a permanent ideological background? John Ralston Saul, Minna Salami, and James Cleverly debate our options.
speaker_desc: James Cleverly is a Conservative politician who has served as Foreign Secretary, Home Secretary, and Education Secretary, as well as Party Chairman. He is currently Shadow Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government. Minna Salami is a writer and social critic whose book Sensuous Knowledge draws on African feminist thought to challenge the dominance of Western epistemology and argue for a more embodied approach to understanding the world. John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and President Emeritus of PEN International. His 16 works, including Voltaire’s Bastards and The Collapse of Globalism , have been translated into 29 languages in 38 countries.
subtitle: What should we be teaching our children?

title: Evolution beyond genes
description: Is evolution truly random, or does it have purpose? Eva Jablonka, author of Evolution in Four Dimensions, challenges the standard story to ask whether living systems can be genuinely goal-directed
speaker_desc: Eva Jablonka, Professor at the Cohn Institute for the History and Philosophy of Science and Ideas at Tel Aviv University, is an evolutionary theorist and geneticist whose work pushes biology beyond a strictly gene-centred view of life.
subtitle: Teleology, consciousness, and want

title: The philosophy of the senses: our inner worlds
description: Philosopher of the senses Barry C. Smith reveals how internal signals from heart, lungs, and gut secretly shape our moods, decisions, and sense of self.
filename: HTLGI2026_H241 Philosophy of the senses HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Barry C. Smith is a professor of philosophy and directs the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study. As founding director of the Centre for the Study of Senses, he has created a platform for collaborative research between philosophers, psychologists and neuroscientists.
subtitle: The limits of digitising sensations

title: Cosmology in crisis
description: New findings—including unexpectedly fast cosmic expansion and mature early galaxies—are challenging our standard cosmology. Do we patch the model, or does this signal a deeper crisis requiring new physics? George Ellis, Claudia de Rham and Bjørn Ekeberg debate
speaker_desc: George Ellis is a South African cosmologist and philosopher of science renowned for bridging the gap between physics and metaphysics. Claudia de Rham is a Swiss theoretical physicist at Imperial College London whose theory of massive gravity proposes that the graviton carries a nonzero mass—offering an alternative account of the universe's accelerating expansion. Bjørn Ekeberg is a Norwegian philosopher of science, author, entrepreneur, and cultural creator whose work challenges orthodox thinking in cosmology, scientific knowledge, and human understanding. Hosted by Jay Shapiro.
subtitle: The smoking gun of the James Webb Telescope

title: Rebalancing the global order
description: Kishore Mahbubani tracks a new shift in global power: Asia is regaining its historical weight, and the West's refusal to accept this reality is fuelling growing conflict.
filename: HTLGI2026_H144 Rebalancing the global order HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Kishore Mahbubani is a Singaporean diplomat and scholar. A former President of the UN Security Council, his work examines the geopolitics of Asia's return to the global centre stage.
subtitle: The rise and fall of Western hegemony

title: The language we speak shapes the way we think, with Lera Boroditsky
description: Cognitive scientist Lera Boroditsky shows how language molds perception of space, time, colour, and causality - and why losing languages is such a pressing problem.
speaker_desc: Lera Boroditsky is a cognitive scientist and linguist whose research has transformed our understanding of how language shapes thought.
subtitle: Why linguistic relativity matters

title: The hidden philosophy of food
description: Philosopher Julian Baggini explores how food shapes identity, ethics, and meaning across cultures—from Japanese precision to Italian conviviality—arguing that understanding humanity starts at the plate.
filename: HTLGI2026_H157 The hidden philosophy of food.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Julian Baggini is a philosopher and author renowned for translating deep philosophical questions into engaging, practical insights. Co-founder of The Philosopher’s Magazine and author of best-sellers such as The Godless Gospel , How the World Thinks , The Virtues of the Table , and The Ego Trick , Baggini defends Enlightenment values and champions reason, scepticism, and humanism in a complex world.
subtitle: The philosophy behind every meal

title: Everything we knew about economics is wrong
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H69 Everything we knew about economics is wrong.HD2.mp4
description: Is economic nationalism a credible theory, or just a set of incoherent policies touted by populist governments? Faiza Shaheen, Maurice Glasman, Llŷr Powell, and Paul Johnson debate.
filename: HTLGI2026_H69 Everything we knew about economics is wrong.HD2.mp4
speaker_desc: Faiza Shaheen is an economist, author, and activist whose work analyses the structural forces behind inequality. She is Executive Director of Tax Justice UK, and the author of Know Your Place . Llŷr Powell is a member of Reform’s shadow cabinet in the recently elected Senedd, where he is responsible for Business and is also Chief Whip. Maurice Glasman is the founder of Blue Labour and a life peer whose political thought draws on Jewish socialism, Christian democracy, and guild association to make the case for a conservatism rooted in working-class culture. Paul Johnson is an economist currently serving as Provost of Queen's College Cambridge, having spent fourteen years as Director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies analysing tax, spending, and public policy across successive governments.
subtitle: Do we need a new economic theory?

title: Reality doesn't care what you think
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H242 Reality doesn't care what you think.SD.mp4
description: Leading sceptic Michael Shermer argues that abandoning the idea of an objective truth is a disastrous mistake.
filename: HTLGI2026_H242 Reality doesn't care what you think.SD.mp4
speaker_desc: Michael Shermer is one of the world's most prominent sceptics and defenders of scientific reason. He's the founding publisher of the widely read Sceptic Magazine, and the executive director of the Sceptics Society.
subtitle: Can we separate fact from fiction?

title: Why you should ignore the Economics Nobel Prize, with Cahal Moran
description: Cahal Moran says economics' "physics envy" for mathematical rigor leaves it detached from reality, masking real declines in living standards, and calls for refocusing on people's needs
speaker_desc: Cahal Moran is a behavioural economist and Visiting Fellow at the London School of Economics and the creator of the YouTube channel Unlearning Economics.
subtitle: From equations back to everyday life

title: The simulation matrix
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/IAI Live 61 The simulation matrix HD.mp4
description: Are simulations revealing truth or just reflecting their creators' biases? John Ioannidis, Paulette Clancy, and Steeve Koonin debate.
filename: IAI Live 61 The simulation matrix HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Paulette Clancy is a Johns Hopkins engineering professor and leading computational materials scientist, pioneering atomic-scale modelling and ML-driven materials discovery. John Ioannidis is a Stanford professor and one of the world’s most-cited scientists, known for reshaping debates on evidence, bias and reproducibility. Steve Koonin is a NYU physicist and former US Undersecretary of Science, known for scrutinising political claims about climate change. Adviser to major science and defence agencies, and author of the controversial Unsettled (2021). Bahar Gholipour hosts.
subtitle: Can a simulation find truth?

title: Memes, minds and the myth of control
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_H249 Memes, minds, and the myth of control.HD2.mp4
description: Do ideas genuinely originate in individuals, or are we merely vessels or hosts for "social contagions"? Tony D. Sampson, Sylvie Delacroix, and Victoria Trumbull debate.
filename: HTLGI2026_H249 Memes, minds, and the myth of control.HD2.mp4
speaker_desc: Tony D. Sampson is an academic and author whose research connects digital culture, media theory, and political philosophy. Victoria Trumbull is a philosopher and writer working across the philosophy of mind and the philosophy of time, whose recent work argues that memory unfolds in time rather than being stored in the brain. Sylvie Delacroix is a scholar and philosopher reimagining how communities might govern shared digital resources in ways that promote fairness, accountability, and trust in the age of AI. Jonny Thomson hosts.
subtitle: Where do our ideas come from?

title: Memory is a construction
description: Neuroscientist Charan Ranganath draws on new research to show that memory is a dynamic, purposeful system which actively reconstructs the past, present, and future.
speaker_desc: Charan Ranganath is Professor of Psychology and Neuroscience and Director of Dynamic Memory Lab at the University of California, Davis, where he spent more than 25 years investigating how the brain encodes, stores and retrieves memories. He is the author of Why We Remember: The Science of Memory and How It Shapes Us .
subtitle: How the brain actively rebuilds memory

title: Rationality can't decide everything for us, with Miriam Schoenfield
description: Should you abandon beliefs shaped by your culture? Epistemologist Miriam Schoenfield argues that every belief system relies on unprovable assumptions.
speaker_desc: Miriam Schoenfield is a leading epistemologist, Associate Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin, and award-winning essayist.
subtitle: How the tools of rationality fail

title: The economics of the new world order
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/IAILIVE2026_63S The economics of the new world order.HD.mp4
description: Leading economist Branko Milanović argues that neoliberalism is ending, replaced by nationalism, tariffs, and trade blocs - and explores the place of the new global middle class within this system.
filename: IAILIVE2026_63S The economics of the new world order.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Formerly a lead research economist at the World Bank, Branko Milanović is one of the world’s leading experts on income inequality and globalization. He is a senior scholar at the Stone Center on Socio-economic Inequality at the City University of New York and is best known for the “Elephant Curve,” a visual representation of how different income groups benefit unevenly from globalization, which has shaped debates on economic development and social justice. Milanović has brought rigorous data analysis and historical insight to some of the most pressing questions of our time. His new book, The Great Global Transformation, examines the decline of neoliberalism and the rise of a new economic order shaped by nationalism, trade conflicts, and shifting power. Drawing on original research, Milanović examines how Asia’s economic growth is reshaping income patterns and the uncertainties facing the global order.
subtitle: The great global transformation

title: The pathology of everyday life
description: Should we see mental health issues as primarily social rather than medical? Anna Lembke, Joanna Moncrieff, and Sarah Wilson debate.
filename: HTLGI2025_L119 The pathology of everyday life.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Anna Lembke is a groundbreaking psychiatrist and addiction medicine expert, best known for her bestselling book, Dopamine Nation. Joanna Moncrieff is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at UCL and was the lead author of a landmark scientific study into the theory of serotonin and depression. She is also a founding member and co-chairperson of the Critical Psychiatry Network. Sarah Wilson is a multi-New York Times and Amazon bestselling author, social philosopher, and philanthropist. She founded the global ‘I Quit Sugar’ movement.
subtitle: The hidden cost of the mental health movement

title: The James Webb Telescope's threat to cosmology
description: Bjørn Ekeberg examines new observations from the James Webb Space Telescope that challenge the standard cosmological story.
speaker_desc: Bjørn Ekeberg is a Norwegian philosopher of science, author, entrepreneur, and cultural creator whose work challenges orthodox thinking in cosmology, scientific knowledge, and human understanding. He holds a Ph.D. in philosophy of science from the University of Victoria (Canada) and has combined rigorous academic inquiry with creative and practical ventures. Ekeberg’s philosophical writing spans cosmology, metaphysics, and the limits of scientific knowledge, exemplified by his book Metaphysical Experiments: Physics and the Invention of the Universe, which critiques assumptions in modern physics and invites fresh perspectives on how we understand the universe.
subtitle: New cracks in our story of the universe

title: Marx, Trump, and a new vision for the Left with Bhaskar Sunkara
description: Jacobin founder Bhaskar Sunkara analyzes the modern left, Trump's tariffs, and why defending liberal democracy is a strategic necessity for socialists.
speaker_desc: Bhaskar Sunkara is the founding editor of Jacobin , the president of the Nation , and the author of The Socialist Manifesto: The Case for Radical Politics in an Era of Extreme Inequality .
subtitle: Is socialism due a revival?

title: Evidence in the dock
description: Can evidence be objectively truthful, or is it merely a persuasive argument in favour of a given theory or narrative? Nick Enfield, Timothy Williamson, Genia Schönbaumsfeld debate.
filename: HTLGI2025_L15 Evidence in the dock HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Nick Enfield is Professor of Linguistics at the University of Sydney and Director of the Sydney Centre for Language Research. He is the author of Language vs Reality. Analytic philosopher and author of Knowledge and Its Limits, Timothy Williamson is a Senior Research Fellow at New College, Oxford and former Wykeham Professor of Logic. Genia Schönbaumsfeld is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Southampton and the author of several books – most recently, Wittgenstein on Religious Belief. In 2023, Genia was awarded a highly prestigious ERC Advanced Grant for her project entitled ‘The Ethics of Doubt – Kierkegaard, Scepticism and Conspiracy Theory’. Jay Shapiro hosts.
subtitle: Calling truth to the stand

title: The Big Bang miracle
description: Despite its central role in modern cosmology, the Big Bang theory originated from religious thought. But do religious assumptions still have a hidden impact on the science? Phil Halper, Joseph Silk, and Priya Natarajan discuss.
filename: HTLGI2025_L6 The big bang miracle HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Phil Halper is a science communicator and Fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society. His recent book, Battle of the Big Bang, explores alternative theories of the universe’s birth, especially those often dismissed for challenging established cosmological ideas. Joseph Silk is a cosmologist and the Savilian Professor of Astronomy Emeritus at the University of Oxford, whose work investigates the early universe, dark matter, and galaxy formation. Priya Natarajan is a Professor of Astrophysics at Yale University and was named as one of Time Magazine's top 100 most influential people in 2024 for her groundbreaking work in the field. Hilary Lawson hosts.
subtitle: Will cosmology ever be truly objective?

title: Privacy is power
description: Political philosopher and AI ethicist Carissa Veliz argues that control over information is control over people: every piece of personal data handed over gives someone else the power to shape your choices, your habits, and even your future.
speaker_desc: Carissa Véliz is a philosopher and Associate Professor at Oxford Univeristy, specialising in AI ethics, privacy and political philosophy. She explores how data and algorithmic prediction shape power, autonomy and democracy.
subtitle: Can democracy survive the rise of digital tech?

title: To save democracy we need fewer elections, with Hélène Landemore
description: Landemore argues true democracy needs fewer elections, not more. Random citizen selection—like jury duty—would break elite capture and reconnect governance to ordinary people, drawing on Athenian precedent that populism gestures toward but misapplies.
speaker_desc: Dedicated to reimagining democracy as a system that truly empowers people, Hélène Landemore is a political philosopher and Professor at Yale University. As founder of Yale’s Citizens’ Assemblies research program and a Distinguished Research Fellow at Oxford’s Institute for Ethics in AI, she blends deep theoretical insight with practical innovation. Landemore challenges traditional electoral democracy by arguing for a more inclusive, deliberative model—one that better captures collective intelligence and democratic reason. Her work, including advising OpenAI’s Democratic Inputs to AI program, explores how democratic institutions can become more stable, representative, and capable of addressing today’s complex political and technological challenges.
subtitle: The ancient Athenian idea that may save democracy

title: The rise and fall of the city
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_L108 The rise and fall of the city.HD.mp4
description: The long urban dominance in elections is fading as a resurgent rural vote reshapes politics. Could remote work and the internet make this shift permanent? Kiran Sidhu, Luís Bettencourt, and Joanna Kavenna discuss.
filename: HTLGI2025_L108 The rise and fall of the city.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Luís Bettencourt is a physicist, author, and urban systems researcher, currently Professor at the University of Chicago and External Professor at the Santa Fe Institute. Kiran Sidhu is an evocative and honest writer known for blending personal insight with lyrical storytelling. She regularly writes for Prospect magazine about rural life and the philosophical implications of this change in her life. Joanna Kavenna is a novelist and travel writer whose work explores themes of place, displacement, and the contrasts between urban and rural existence. She's held the Alistair Horne Fellowship at St Antony’s College Oxford and the Harper-Wood at St John’s College Cambridge.
subtitle: The politics of place

title: The patriarchy in question
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_L120 The patriarchy in question HD [Shortened Intro].mp4
description: Are feminist gains under threat? As boys are outperformed by girls at every school level, and women in their 20s out-earn men, there are increasing signs of anti-feminist backlash on the Right. Catherine Hakim, Mary Ann Sieghardt, Paul Dolan, and Nick Fletcher debate the consequences.
filename: HTLGI2025_L120 The patriarchy in question HD [Shortened Intro].mp4
speaker_desc: Paul Dolan is a behavioural scientist and happiness expert at LSE, widely known for his research on wellbeing, decision-making, and human motivation. Nick Fletcher is a former Tory MP for Don Valley known for his opinions on gender equality, trans issues and immigration. He was chair of the Men and Boys All-Party Parliamentary Group. Catherine Hakim is a social scientist and author specialising in women's employment and women's issues, known for inventing the concept of "erotic capital". Mary Ann Sieghart is an author, broadcaster and former Times columnist whose work focuses on gender equality, political analysis, and public policy. Avantika Chilkoti hosts.
subtitle: Has feminism left men behind?

title: Iain McGilchrist on why the mind is not a machine
description: Iain McGilchrist argues that explaining the mind in purely mechanistic terms is a profound mistake, rooted in materialist and reductionist assumptions.
speaker_desc: Iain McGilchrist is a distinguished British neuroscientist, psychiatrist and philosopher. A former Fellow of All Souls College, Oxford, he has also worked as a consulting psychiatrist, and is known for his influential work on the relationship between the structure of our brains, human cultures and our understanding of the world.
subtitle: The end of materialism

title: How to sue your government, with Jolyon Maugham
description: Jolyon Maugham, the barrister who took on Boris Johnson, argues that laywers need to intervene in a legal system which too often fails to hold those in power to account.
speaker_desc: Jolyon Maugham KC is an activist barrister, founder of the Good Law Project, and thorn in the side of the government. Jolyon has sought to challenge the UK government's approach to Brexit, Covid and transgender rights. He has written for the Telegraph, Guardian and New Statesman on the legal implications of Brexit.
subtitle: The fight to democratise justice

title: Imagination and the real
description: Neuroscience increasingly suggests that perception and imagination share the same brain processes. Does this mean that reality and hallucination are indistinguishable? Neuroscientists Karl Friston, Maria Balaet, and Nadine Dijkstra discuss.
speaker_desc: Nadine Dijkstra is Principal Investigator at UCL’s Queen Square Institute of Neurology, where she leads the Imagine Reality Lab in exploring how the brain constructs our sense of reality. Karl Friston is a world-leading neuroscientist and Professor at UCL, best known as the architect of the influential Free Energy Principle and a Principal Research Fellow with the Wellcome Trust. Maria Balaet is a leading voice in psychedelic research, using advanced neuroimaging at King’s College London to uncover how these substances transform consciousness. Hosted by Claudia Canavan.
subtitle: Could reality be a controlled hallucination?

title: Love is more than magic
description: Philosopher Alain de Botton explores how romantic ideals mislead us and why emotional maturity, not chemistry, holds the key to enduring intimacy.
speaker_desc: Alain de Botton is the bestselling philosopher redefining how we understand love, work, and meaning in the modern world. He first rose to prominence with Essays in Love, a novel-philosophy hybrid that became an international bestseller. He has since authored several bestselling works that blend literary elegance, psychological insight, and philosophical depth.
subtitle: Why romantic idealism fails us

title: Navigating the unknown
description: If science builds models rather than revealing truth — as Heisenberg and Hawking argued — and they still work, what does that say about our grasp on reality? Graham Priest, Jessica Frazier and Hilary Lawson debate.
speaker_desc: Graham Priest is Professor of Philosophy at City University of New York. He is well known for his work on non-classical logic and Buddhist Philosophy. Jessica Frazier is an Oxford philosopher who works on Indian Philosophy and the European tradition of phenomenology. She is also a frequent consultant for the BBC and speaker on In Our Time. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything , has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Shini Somara hosts.
subtitle: The weeds within the theory of truth

title: Where quantum meets gravity, with Ivette Fuentes
description: Can smaller, cheaper experiments unlock quantum gravity? Physicist Yvette Fuentes thinks so — and she's building one, inspired by Roger Penrose's ideas on gravitational wave function collapse.
speaker_desc: Ivette Fuentes is a Professor of Quantum Physics at the University of Southampton and an Emmy Fellow at Keble College, University of Oxford. She earned her PhD in physics from the University of Nottingham and completed postdoctoral research at the University of Vienna, where she worked extensively on quantum optics and relativistic quantum information theory. Fuentes has since established herself as a leading figure in the study of quantum gravity, focusing on how quantum phenomena behave in curved spacetime — bridging quantum mechanics with general relativity.
subtitle: Could tabletop experiments be the future?

title: Technology is always political, with Sheila Jasanoff
description: Groundbreaking science and technology theorist Sheila Jasanoff argues that technology isn't neutral or inevitable: our social choices actively create the technological world we inhabit.
speaker_desc: Sheila Sen Jasanoff is an Indian-American academic in the field of Science and Technology Studies. In 2021 she was elected to the American Philosophical Society. Her research has been recognized with many awards, including the 2022 Holberg Prize "for her groundbreaking research in science and technology studies."
subtitle: Technocrats and codes of social understanding

title: In the name of reason
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_L13 In the name of reason HD.mp4
description: Reason doesn't always free us from bias — it can sharpen our ability to justify existing beliefs, making educated people more prone to groupthink. But can it be reclaimed as a tool for critical resistance rather than tribal conformity? Dan Sperber, Steve Fuller, and Miriam Schoenfield discuss.
filename: HTLGI2025_L13 In the name of reason HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Dan Sperber is a distinguished anthropologist and philosopher who is the author of several critically-acclaimed books, including The Enigma of Reason. Steve Fuller is a professor of sociology at the University of Warwick. He is the author of dozens of books, including Post-truth: Knowledge as a Power Game. Miriam Schoenfield is a leading epistemologist, Associate Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin, and award-winning essayist. Jack Symes is a public philosopher and writer. He is the producer of The Panpsycast Philosophy Podcast and editor of the Bloomsbury series Talking about Philosophy. He is currently Teacher and Researcher at Durham University, UK.
subtitle: Is rationality really a social good?

title: The world after liberalism
description: Maurice Glasman and Sohrab Amari diagnose the roots of the current crisis of liberalism and explore possibilities for what lies beyond it.
speaker_desc: Political theorist, Labour life peer, and a member of the House of Lords, Maurice Glasman is the founder of the Blue Labour movement in 2009. Co-founder of Compact magazine and author of Tyranny, Inc., Sohrab Ahmari is a celebrated journalist and cultural critic.
subtitle: Moving beyond the myth of the individual

title: Riches and rags
description: Should we prioritise eradicating poverty or is wealth equality essential for justice? Join Yaron Brook, Ingrid Robeyns, and Thangam Debbonaire in debate.
speaker_desc: Ingrid Robeyns is a philosopher and economist best known for developing limitarianism, the case for placing ethical limits on personal wealth. She holds the Chair of Ethics in Institutions at Utrecht University. Yaron Brook is an entrepreneur and political commentator, best known as chairman of the Ayn Rand Institute and host of The Yaron Brook Show. He co-authored the bestseller Free Market Revolution. Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords, having served for nine years as MP for Bristol West and as a senior figure in Keir Starmer’s Shadow Cabinet. Avantika Chilkoti hosts.
subtitle: Are we wrong to worry about wealth inequality?

title: Science beyond the physical
description: Science has long assumed reality is purely physical — but could materialism actually be holding back progress on neuroscience, quantum gravity, and the origin of life? Lisa Feldman Barrett, Michael Levin, and Adam Frank discuss.
speaker_desc: Lisa Feldman Barrett is among the most cited scientists in the world for her research on the psychology and neuroscience of emotions. Adam Frank is an astrophysicist who explores the origins of stars, civilizations and consciousness, and is a leading figure in astrobiology and the search for alien life. Michael Levin is a synthetic biologist whose pioneering work in regenerative biology involves building biological robots to probe the nature of life, intelligence and evolution. Güneş Taylor hosts.
subtitle: Is materialism becoming obsolete?

title: The fight for the AI economy
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_L43 The fight for the AI economy.HD new.mp4
description: Two visions of the AI future collide in this head-to-head debate: Zoltan Istvan's tech-optimist 'Automated Abundance Economy' and Aaron Bastani's 'Fully Automated Luxury Communism.'
filename: HTLGI2025_L43 The fight for the AI economy.HD new.mp4
speaker_desc: Transhumanist thinker and former US presidential candidate, Zoltan Istvan is known for promoting life extension and emerging technologies in politics. Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media, described as 'the slickest of the guerrilla news and opinion operations that have sprung up in Britain' by the Guardian .
subtitle: Visions of an automated future

title: The end of woke
description: Where did woke culture come from—and is it finished? Prof. Eric Kaufmann traces its roots and argues the left needs a new political framework to survive.
speaker_desc: Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at the University of Buckingham and Director of the Centre for Heterodox Social Science. His research focuses on political demography, national identity, immigration, and cultural change.
subtitle: A 'vibe shift' in mass media

title: The only freedom which deserves the name
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_L59 The only freedom which deserves the name HD [NEW INTRO].mp4
description: Minna Salami, Yascha Mounk, and Curtis Yarvin debate whether liberalism can still claim the moral high ground, or whether it is just one partisan worldview among many.
filename: HTLGI2025_L59 The only freedom which deserves the name HD [NEW INTRO].mp4
speaker_desc: Curtis Yarvin, described as "The Philosopher Behind J.D. Vance," argues that democracy is a failed experiment and should be replaced by monarchy. Expert on the challenges facing liberal democracy in the 21st century, Yascha Mounk is a political scientist and Professor at Johns Hopkins University. Writer, social critic, and thought leader Minna Salami is known for fusing feminism, philosophy, and political thought. She is the author of Can Feminism Be African?.
subtitle: Can liberalism survive the century?

title: Mental health and the chemical imbalance myth
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_H155 Mental health and chemical imbalance myth.HD.mp4
description: Psychiatrist Joanna Moncrieff argues that the chemical imbalance theory of depression lacks scientific support, despite prompting the widespread use of antidepressants.
filename: HTLGI2025_H155 Mental health and chemical imbalance myth.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Joanna Moncrieff is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at University College London, and a consultant psychiatrist for the NHS. She is also a founding member and co-chairperson of the Critical Psychiatry Network. Her most recent book is Chemically Imbalanced: The Making and Unmaking of the Serotonin Myth.
subtitle: Exposing the shaky science behind antidepressants

title: The OnlyFans paradox, with Farha Khalidi
description: Feminist cultural commentator Farha Khalidi argues that the moral panic over OnlyFans conceals centuries of double standards over sex work.
speaker_desc: Farha Khalidi is a feminist cultural commentator, TikToker and OnlyFans model with 1.7 million followers on TikTok.
subtitle: Misogyny, double standards and the sex work debate

title: The mirror
description: The mirror has long symbolised art and the mind's relationship to reality - but can we, or should we seek to copy the world at all? Dean Rickles, Winsome Pinnock, and Joanna Kavenna discuss.
speaker_desc: Dean Rickles is historian and philosopher of Modern Physics at the University of Sydney, where he is also a director of the Sydney Centre for Time. He investigates the frontiers of quantum gravity, string theory and the philosophy of the mind. Winsome Pinnock is a British playwright and dramaturge, known for her pioneering contributions to contemporary theatre. Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning writer. She is the author of six books and has written for The New Yorker, The Guardian and London Review of Books. Hosted by Jessica Frazier.
subtitle: Can art and thought mirror reality?

title: Mysticism vs modernity
description: David Pearce, Naomi Goulder, and Rupert Sheldrake debate whether the battle between science and spirituality will ever truly be resolved.
speaker_desc: Transhumanist philosopher David Pearce, author of Philosophy of Action Naomi Goulder, and world-renowned biologist Rupert Sheldrake debate mysticism and modernity. Hosted by Jay Shapiro.
subtitle: Spirituality makes a comeback

title: The Enlightenment under fire, with John Gray and Hilary Lawson
description: Join John Gray and Hilary Lawson in conversation on the power of philosophy as a disruptive force and the growing challenges to the liberal belief in progress.
speaker_desc: One of Britain’s most provocative thinkers, John Gray is a political philosopher famous for dismantling liberalism and exposing the illusions of human progress. Former Professor of European Thought at the London School of Economics, Gray has challenged orthodoxy across the political spectrum with a body of work that ranges from critiques of Enlightenment rationalism to meditations on the limits of secular humanism. He is the bestselling author of Straw Dogs, The Silence of Animals , and Seven Types of Atheism as well as a frequent contributor to The Guardian , New Statesman, and The Times Literary Supplement . Gray’s sharp insights and contrarian stance continue to shape contemporary debates on ethics, politics, and the future of humanity.
subtitle: Human nature, truth, and the decline of liberalism

title: Global challenge and global action
description: Liberal democracies face mounting climate failures as emissions rise and political will wavers. Can they adapt, or does the crisis demand an entirely new political model? James Bacchus, Leah Downey, and Kai Heron discuss.
filename: HTLGI2025_L5 Global challenge and global action.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: James Bacchus is a professor of Global Affairs and Director of the Global Economic and Environmental Opportunity Centre at the University of Central Florida. With a long and storied career in Congress and the World Trade Organisation (WTO), his most recent work argues that we need global democracy in order to have true, sustainable development. Leah Downey is a political theorist, a junior research fellow at St. John’s College, Cambridge and a lecturer at Kings College London. She has published research on the macroeconomics of the green transition and is the author of Our Money: Monetary Policy as if Democracy Matters . Kai Heron is a political organiser, trade unionist, and Lecturer in Political Ecology at Lancaster University. He is the co-editor of the De Gruyter Degrowth Handbook , has published widely on the politics of green energy and is the co-author of Radical Abundance: How to Win a Green Democratic Future . Adrienne Buller hosts.
subtitle: Can liberal democracies face the climate crisis?

title: Our future theories of the universe
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_L29 Our future theories of the universe.HD.mp4
description: Roger Penrose & Brian Cox explore whether flaws in foundational scientific theories—from the Big Bang to consciousness—are insurmountable or can be overcome to reshape our understanding of reality.
filename: HTLGI2025_L29 Our future theories of the universe.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on black holes, Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician and physicist. In recent years, he has investigated the relationship between physics and the mind, famously arguing that quantum mechanics plays an essential role in solving the mysteries of human consciousness. Penrose has made numerous appearances on media such as BBC, Closer to Truth, and The Joe Rogan Experience. In 1994, he was knighted for his services to science. Famed for his poetic take on the cosmos, physicist and broadcaster Brian Cox has become one of the world’s most recognizable voices in science communication. A former musician turned particle physicist, Cox has played a key role in major experiments at CERN and the Large Hadron Collider, while also captivating millions through BBC series such as Wonders of the Universe, The Planets, and Forces of Nature. Cox has been showered with praise for his contributions, appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE), and is the recipient of the Institute of Physics Kelvin Medal and the Michael Faraday Prize. Beyond his work as a Royal Society professor of physics at the University of Manchester, Cox advocates for public scientific literacy and political responsibility in science funding. His style blends rigorous physics with a deep sense of awe — bringing relativity, entropy, and quantum theory into living rooms around the globe. His rare ability to fuse clarity with wonder has earned global acclaim.
subtitle: Brian Cox interviews Roger Penrose

title: Democracy in the ruins of neoliberalism
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/IAILIVE2025_58S Democracy in the ruins of neoliberalism.HD.mp4
description: Philosophers Wendy Brown and Sophie Scott-Brown explore how antidemocratic politics and neoliberal economics intertwine.
filename: IAILIVE2025_58S Democracy in the ruins of neoliberalism.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Wendy Brown is one of the most influential political theorists of her generation, known for her penetrating analyses of power, neoliberalism, democracy, and the fate of the public good in contemporary political life. Brown is currently the UPS Foundation Professor in the School of Social Science at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton and Professor Emerita of Political Science at the University of California, Berkeley. Hosted by Sophie Scott-Brown.
subtitle: Nihilism, populism, and political renewal

title: The wealth cap
description: Philosopher Ingrid Robeyns proposes the idea of limitarianism to address soaring inequality, setting a hard cap on the wealth of the ultra-rich.
speaker_desc: Ingrid Robeyns is a political philosopher known for her work on economic justice, the capability approach, and limits on extreme wealth.
subtitle: A bold case for limiting extreme wealth

title: The price of populism, with Jason Furman
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/IAI Live 58ST The price of populism with Jason Furman HD.mp4.mp4
description: Ex-Obama advisor Jason Furman argues that the line between business and government is becoming increasingly blurred under the Trump administration.
filename: IAI Live 58ST The price of populism with Jason Furman HD.mp4.mp4
speaker_desc: Jason Furman is a prominent American economist known for his extensive contributions to public policy, academia, and economic analysis. He currently serves as the Aetna Professor of the Practice of Economic Policy at Harvard University. He served as the Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA) under President Barack Obama from August 2013 to January 2017. In this role, he acted as a principal economic advisor to the President.
subtitle: The hidden costs of Trump's economic promises

title: I forget therefore I am
description: Forgetting may matter more than memory: it shapes identity, enables decisions, and supports wellbeing. Those unable to forget show its vital role — but should therapy focus on letting go rather than recovering the past?
filename: IAILIVE2026_60 I forget therefore I am.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Join Oliver Hardt, Professor of Psychology at McGill University, Catherine Loveday, Author of The Secret World of the Brain, and Iain McGilchrist, famed neuroscientist, philosopher and psychologist at the University of Oxford as they clash over what it means to be human. Hosted by Oxford philosopher Jessica Frazier.
subtitle: Is memory essential to who we are?

title: How to reclaim the body
description: Psycholanalyst and author of Fat is a Feminist Issue, Susie Orbach, argues that society needs to revalue bodily autonomy and redefine the self beyond appearance.
filename: HTLGI2024_L42 How to relcaim the body.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Susie Orbach is a psychotherapist, psychoanalyst, and social critic. She came to prominence with the book Fat Is A Feminist Issue, and was therapist to Diana, Princess of Wales.
subtitle: Moving beyond the beauty industry

title: AI and the mysteries of reality
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_H169 AI and the mysteries of reality.HD.mp4
description: While some argue that AI will produce a new golden age of scientific discovery, critics claim that it cannot independently define problems or create truly novel insights. Will AI ever truly discover on its own? Roman Yampolskiy, Steve Fuller, and Suzanne Livingston discuss.
filename: HTLGI2025_H169 AI and the mysteries of reality.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Computer scientist Roman Yampolskiy, philosopher Steve Fuller, and co-curator of AI: More than Human Suzanne Livingston debate whether AI can make novel scientific discoveries. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
subtitle: The future of scientific discovery

title: Thinking isn't only in the brain, with Barbara Tversky
description: Cognitive psychologist Barbara Tversky argues that thinking is spatial and embodied, not merely verbal: gestures shape thought, and abstract ideas are rooted in bodily experience.
speaker_desc: Barbara Tversky is an active Emerita Professor of Psychology at Stanford and Professor of Psychology at Columbia Teachers College. Her research has spanned memory, categorization, language, spatial cognition, event perception and cognition, diagrammatic reasoning, sketching, creativity, design, and gesture. The overall goals have been to uncover how people think about the spaces they inhabit and the actions they perform and see and then how people use the world and the things in it. Her 2019 book, Mind in Motion: How Action Shapes Thought, provides an overview of some of that work. She has collaborated widely, with linguists, philosophers, neuroscientists, computer scientists, chemists, biologists, architects, designers, and artists.
subtitle: How the body shapes the mind

title: Peace, passion and adventure
description: Is peace actually a virtue, or does it lead to stagnation? Explore the dark side of serenity with Janne Teller, Alenka Zupančič, and Paul Bloom as they debate if we need enemies to find meaning.
filename: HTLGI2025_H160 Peace, passion and adventure HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Janne Teller was formerly a UN macroeconomist specialising in developing economies. She has since become a bestselling author of novels, essays, and short stories. Alenka Zupančič is a leading Lacanian philosopher and social theorist. She is a professor at The European Graduate School and at the University of Nova Gorica. Paul Bloom is a Canadian-American psychologist, bestselling author, and celebrated speaker. He is Professor Emeritus at Yale and a professor at the University of Toronto. Bloom’s work explores human nature, morality, and pleasure.
subtitle: The comfort of chaos

title: The iron fist vs the invisible hand
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_L12 The iron fist vs the invisible hand v2 HD.mp4
description: Does democracy hinder economic growth? Curtis Yarvin, Aaron Bastani, and Hélène Landemore debate if authoritarian models like China are the future of global wealth.
filename: HTLGI2025_L12 The iron fist vs the invisible hand v2 HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Curtis Yarvin, described as "The Philosopher Behind J.D. Vance," argues that democracy is a failed experiment and should be replaced by monarchy. Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media, described by the Guardian as 'the slickest of the guerrilla news and opinion operations that have sprung up in Britain’. Hélène Landemore is a political philosopher and professor at Yale University, and is also a Distinguished Research Fellow at Oxford’s Institute for Ethics in AI.
subtitle: The new economic order

title: There is no fundamental basis to reality, with James Ladyman and Susan Schneider
description: Why the "bottom" of reality might not exist. James Ladyman and Susan Schneider debate the nature of existence and why we are losing the competition with AI goals.
speaker_desc: Susan Schneider is an American philosopher and cognitive scientist, known for her work on the nature of consciousness, artificial intelligence, and the future of mind. She is the founding director of the Center for the Future Mind at Florida Atlantic University and holds the Baruch S. Blumberg NASA/Library of Congress Chair in Astrobiology, Exploration, and Scientific Innovation. Schneider is best known for her exploration of post-biological intelligence and the philosophical implications of machine consciousness. In her widely discussed book Artificial You: AI and the Future of Your Mind, she examines whether machines could ever truly possess consciousness, and whether humans should merge with them. James Ladyman is a pioneering philosopher renowned for combining rigorous natural science with deep metaphysical inquiry. A leader in philosophy of science and physics, he champions ontic structural realism, the view that reality is fundamentally relational, and defends a naturalised metaphysics that aligns with our best scientific understanding, challenging inherited intuitions that mislead us about the nature of the universe. In Everything Must Go: Metaphysics Naturalized, Ladyman argues that many common metaphysical assumptions—about objects, causation, or essence—are relics incompatible with modern science. Ladyman’s fusion of analytic clarity with scientific insight reshapes how we think about reality—revealing a cosmos that is stranger and more beautiful than our unexamined instincts suggest.
subtitle: Physics, AI and the structure of everything

title: Dreams of the future
description: Should we give up on the notion that the future will be better than the past? In a time when such optimism seems to be fading, Daniel Markovits, Eric Kaufmann and Thangam Debbonaire discuss the value of the future.
speaker_desc: Daniel Markovits is the Guido Calabresi Professor of Law at Yale Law School and the author of the best-selling book, The Meritocracy Trap . Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords, chair of the Labour Women's Network, and a leading voice on cultural policy. Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at The University of Buckingham and Director of the Centre for Heterodox Social Science. Hosted by Jack Symes.
subtitle: Are visions of progress coming to an end?

title: Materialism and emergence can't explain consciousness, with Alex O'Connor
description: Alex O'Connor critiques materialism and emergence theory, arguing that physical processes alone cannot explain consciousness. Discover the case for seeing consciousness as a fundamental property of the universe.
speaker_desc: Alex O’Connor is a YouTuber, public speaker, writer, and host of the Within Reason Podcast. He first began posting videos to his YouTube channel "CosmicSkeptic" before taking his degree in philosophy and theology at St John's College, Oxford. He has since grown his following to over 1.5 million subscribers with his rigorous yet accessible philosophy videos. O’Connor has appeared on television programmes such as Piers Morgan Uncensored, BBC Sunday Morning Live, and Channel 4 News. He has debated philosophy, religion, free speech, and more with leading thinkers Slavoj Žižek, Richard Dawkins, Neil deGrasse Tyson, and more.
subtitle: From new atheism to panpsychism

title: The power and politics of shame
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2026_L27 The power and politics of shame.HD_1.mp4
description: Kenneth Roth, former director of Human Rights Watch, illustrates moral pressure and strategic shaming can compel even repressive regimes to change.
filename: HTLGI2026_L27 The power and politics of shame.HD_1.mp4
