Jessica Frazier is a philosopher at the University of Oxford and Fellow of the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies. She is an expert on Indian Philosophy and the European tradition of phenomenology. Phil Collins hosts.
subtitle: Science, philosophy or religion: which story wins?

title: The trouble with meritocracy
description: Professor Daniel Markovits argues that meritocratic societies are fundamentally flawed, succumbing to economic stagnation and societal decay.

His best-selling book, The Meritocracy Trap: How America's Foundational Myth Feeds Inequality, Dismantles the Middle Class, and Devours the Elite, has sparked a significant discussion about the problems inherent in meritocratic societies.

title: How to hack the reality simulation, with Roman Yampolskiy

speaker_desc: Roman Yampolskiy is a professor and computer scientist at the University of Louisville who specialises in artificial intelligence, AI safety, digital forensics and behavioural biometrics. He is the author of Considerations on the AI Endgame.
subtitle: Can intelligence escape its own universe?

title: Mental health in an age of over-diagnosis
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_H233 Mental health in an age of over diagnosis.HD.mp4
description: Is mental illness being over-diagnosed? Psychiatrist Alastair Santhouse explores how culture and science have expanded mental health labels, blurring the line between normal and unhealthy.

speaker_desc: Alastair Santhouse is a consultant psychiatrist with over 20 years of experience at Guy's Hospital and the Maudsley Hospital in London. A sharp public intellectual, Liu is best known for her incisive critiques of elite liberalism, academic hypocrisy, and the commodification of virtue. She brings together Marxist cultural analysis with polemic flair, offering a compelling—and at times confrontational—challenge to the moral self-image of the contemporary professional class.
subtitle: From identity politics to class struggle

title: The Left's identity crisis
description: Is the Left shifting from compassionate welfarism to a more hard-nosed politics focused on productivity? Maurice Glasman, Bhaskar Sunkara and Pam Cox discuss.
speaker_desc: Maurice Glasman is a political theorist, Labour life peer, and founder of the Blue Labour movement in 2009. Pam Cox is the Labour MP for Colchester who was recently elected to Parliament in 2024. Prior to this she was a professor of social history and criminology at the University of Essex and a fellow of the Royal Society of Arts. Bhaskar Sunkara is currently the president of The Nation, the oldest continuously published weekly magazine in the United States. He is a former vice-chair of the Democratic Socialists of America and the author of The Socialist Manifesto. Roger Hearing hosts.
subtitle: Woke vs work

title: The life and philosophy of Jeremy Corbyn

speaker_desc: Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour Party's leader from 2015 to 2020. Representing the constituency of Islington North since 1983, he was a vocal backbencher with a reputation of voting against his party until he was elected leader with the largest party membership for a generation. He contested the 2017 general election and won 40% of the vote, the largest Labour share since 2001. Since he has been expelled from the Labour Party, Jeremy has gone on to win his Islington seat as an independent and has recently been elected the parliamentary leader of Your Party, a party he founded with fellow MP Zarah Sultana. His views place him firmly on the progressive left where he is staunchly anti-war, anti-austerity, pro-nationalisation and pro-Palestine. In the current Parliament, Jeremy is a key opponent to Keir Starmer, holding the government to account from the left.
subtitle: A life on the Left

title: The end of ideology
description: Sam Kiley, Glenn Greenwald and Seyla Benhabib discuss whether geopolitics is witnessing the end of ideology and the return of raw geography.
speaker_desc: Glenn Greenwald is a Pulitzer-prize winning journalist, known for publishing the Snowden files and uncovering the largest corruption scandal in Brazil's history. One of the most influential political philosophers of her generation, Seyla Benhabib is Senior Research Scholar at Columbia Law School and has shaped global debates on democracy, migration, and human rights. Sam Kiley is a multi-award winning journalist currently working as World Affairs Editor of The Independent and has covered conflict for more than 30 years, reporting from the front lines in Afghanistan, Iraq and Somalia, among other war zones.
subtitle: Power, geography and the global order

title: Forgiving the unforgivable
description: Professor Lucy Allais argues true forgiveness is radical: forgiving even “unforgivable” acts without excuses or amends. It means refusing to define people by their worst actions and seeing them as capable of moral growth.
speaker_desc: Lucy Allais is Professor of Philosophy at Johns Hopkins University and the University of the Witwatersrand, renowned for her work on Immanuel Kant, forgiveness, punishment, and bioethics. She is the author of Manifest Reality: Kant's Idealism and His Realism.
subtitle: The true meaning of forgiveness

title: All the world's a stage
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_H108 All the world's a stage HD.mp4
description: Claire Blencowe, Michelle Terry, and Paul Bloom discuss whether it is possible to stop performing our own identity - and whether there is even a "true self" at all.
filename: HTLGI2025_H108 All the world's a stage HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Claire Blencowe is an associate professor of Sociology and co-chair of the Just Eco-Geo-Political Futures research group at Warwick University. She is a leading scholar of Foucault. Michelle Terry is an Olivier Award-winning actor and the Artistic Director of Shakespeare's Globe, where she has gained critical acclaim for her modern interpretations of Shakespeare's plays. Matthew Taylor is a British former political strategist and current Chief Executive of the Royal Society for the Encouragement of Arts, Manufactures and Commerce.
subtitle: Performance and the search for the true self

title: Glenn Greenwald: Trump's Iran attacks are business as usual for the US
description: Pulizter Prize-winning journalist Glenn Greenwald argues that Trump's war with Iran is in line with the US's existing foreign policy strategy, rather than a deviation from it.
speaker_desc: After founding a law firm concentrating on First Amendment litigation (protecting free speech and a free press), Glenn Greenwald turned to journalism. He became a vocal critic of the Iraq War and American foreign policy, a position he has maintained. He started contributing to Salon in 2007 and to The Guardian in 2012, and in the latter published a series of reports detailing covert American and British global surveillance programmes based on classified documents provided by Edward Snowden. For this work, his team won a Pulitzer Prize. Glenn Greenwald has written multiple best-selling books, including How Would a Patriot Act and No Place to Hide: Edward Snowden, the NSA, and the U.S. Surveillance State . He now hosts System Update , where he has interviewed academics, political figures, and commentators including Jeffrey Sachs, John Mearsheimer, Edward Snowden, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and many others.
subtitle: A new phase in interventionist foreign policy

title: The structure of consciousness
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_L100 The structure of consciousness v2 HD.mp4
description: Do modern theories in neuroscience support the idea that perception is neutral data about the world, or do they suggest that our brains actively construct the reality we experience—and what does that mean for the existence of the self? filename: HTLGI2025_L100 The structure of consciousness v2 HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Karl Friston is Professor of Imaging Neuroscience at University College London and Principal Research Fellow for the Wellcome Trust. Jan Westerhoff is Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at Oxford University. He researches the philosophical aspects of the religious traditions of ancient India, and contemporary analytic metaphysics. Susan Schneider is an American philosopher and cognitive scientist, known for her work on the nature of consciousness, artificial intelligence, and the future of mind.
subtitle: Questioning our relation to reality and the self

title: How the Right won the culture war
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2025_H164 How the right won the culture war.HD.mp4
description: Inaya Folarin Iman argues that there is a growing multiracial political base which rejects the identity politics of the Leftand embraces the cultural populism of the Right.

Recently, she has focused on challenging the dominance of identity politics in public discourse and advocating for policies rooted in shared humanity rather than divisive rhetoric. Her work at the Equiano Project emphasizes the need for critical reflection on how society addresses complex issues like racial inequality and multiculturalism. She argues for open debate on topics often constrained by political correctness, such as integration and cultural identity. She was a regular presenter on GB news and is also a regular writer for Spiked Online , the Telegraph , and the Daily Mail .
subtitle: The contradictions within woke politics

title: Atomic dreams and nuclear nightmares

description: Tim Gregory, Sheila Jasanoff, and M.V. Ramana debate the risks and promise of nuclear power: is it our best hope of delivering clean, reliable energy, or an expensive and dangerous distraction?

speaker_desc: Ken Roth is an attorney, activist and author best known as the Executive Director of Human Rights Watch for nearly thirty years. speaker_desc: Lionel Shriver is an American author and journalist best known for her 2003 novel We Need to Talk About Kevin , which won the Orange Prize for Fiction. subtitle: The post-rational reign of mania

subtitle: Why psychiatry should move past chemical imbalance

subtitle: How to find meaning in an age of collapse

subtitle: The hidden assumptions that limit our theories

She is a lecturer in Philosophy at the University of East Anglia and former director at the Europaeum Institute at the University of Oxford. Rana Mitter hosts.
subtitle: Can belonging exist without exclusion?

title: The one and the many
description: Is reality best understood as a unified whole or as a collection of separate parts, and can science or philosophy ever coherently explain how the two fit together? Physicists Sabine Hossenfelder, Ivette Fuentes and James Ladyman discuss.

Hosted by Jack Symes.
subtitle: Is the universe a seamless unity?

subtitle: Can machines ever be conscious?

description: Martha Fiennes, Josh Cohen and Joanna Kavenna discuss whether, in the aftermath of modernism and postmodernism, literature should attempt to represent portray realistic events.
speaker_desc: Martha Fiennes is an award-winning filmmaker and pioneering AI artist, known for Onegin, Chromophobia, and her AI-driven work Yugen, which has been showcased from Venice to the Serpentine Gallery. Josh Cohen established himself as an academic in American literature and critical theory, before deciding to train as a psychoanalyst. title: The chains of freedom

He is the author of the bestselling book The Meritocracy Trap Elizabeth Anderson is Professor of Public Philosophy, Politics and Economics at the University of Michigan. Yaron Brook is an entrepreneur, writer, activist, and political scientist. He is currently chairman of the board of the Ayn Rand Institute and host of the Yaron Brook Show. Isabel Hilton hosts.
subtitle: Is freedom a universal good?

title: Europe's last chance
description: From the war in Ukraine to Trump’s tariff threats, crises are shaking Europe. Timothy Garton Ash argues they offer a chance to renew, unite, and defend liberal democracy.

subtitle: Leading with love

description: Catherine Hakim argues that beauty, sex appeal, and social skills form “erotic capital,” a powerful asset society often ignores, yet one that strongly shapes gender, power, and equality debates.

speaker_desc: Catherine Hakim is a social scientist and author specializing in women’s employment and gender issues, with over 100 papers and numerous books published.

Sir Vernon Bogdanor is a British political scientist and constitutional expert. He is a research professor of Contemporary British History at King's College London.

title: Neighbours before strangers
description: Alain de Botton, Seyla Benhabib, and Tommy Curry discuss whether universalism wrongly ignores natural partiality to those close to us, or whether it remains essential to Western values.
speaker_desc: Alain de Botton is the best-selling philosopher and founder of The School of Life, an organisation dedicated to developing emotional intelligence through philosophy, psychotherapy, and culture. Tommy Curry is the Personal Chair of Africana Philosophy and Black Male Studies at the University of Edinburgh, renowned for his critical scholarship on the intersection of race, gender, and power. Alex O'Connor hosts.

description: Sparta prized the body, Athens the mind, and the West chose Athens. But today, declining reasoning, AI-outsourced thinking, and body fixation raise doubts about an intellect-led age.

Anders Sandberg is a Swedish researcher, futurist, and transhumanist renowned for his work on human enhancement and future technologies. He served as a senior research fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute and the Oxford Martin School at the University of Oxford. His research encompasses societal and ethical implications of emerging technologies, cognitive enhancement, and existential risks. David Pearce is a British philosopher best known for his advocacy of the abolitionist project, the ethical vision of using advanced science and technology to eliminate suffering in all sentient life. A co-founder of the World Transhumanist Association (now Humanity+), he authored The Hedonistic Imperative, a manifesto that argues for the use of genetic engineering, nanotechnology, and neuroscience to replace the biological substrates of pain with gradients of intelligent bliss.
subtitle: Could Ancient Greece guide our future?

title: How brains construct reality, with Karl Friston
description: Friston argues the brain predicts rather than mirrors reality. Under the Free Energy Principle, it minimizes surprise by updating beliefs or acting, so perception and action construct the world.
speaker_desc: Karl Friston is a neuroscientist and theoretical neurobiologist best known for developing the Free Energy Principle, a unifying framework for understanding brain function, perception, and action. He is Professor of Imaging Neuroscience at University College London and a leading figure in computational psychiatry, cognitive neuroscience, and the philosophy of mind.
subtitle: Uncertainty shapes consciousness

title: Living without limits
description: Anna Lembke, Federico Campagna and Barry Schwartz debate whether moderation enriches life or suppresses authenticity. They explore addiction, excess and meaning in a world engineered for stimulation.
speaker_desc: Anna Lembke is a groundbreaking psychiatrist and addiction medicine expert at Stanford. She is author of Drug Dealer MD and most recently Dopamine Nation which argues that too much pleasure in the short time leads to pain in the long-term. Federico Campagna is a leading philosopher, metaphysician and expert on Nihilism. His book Technic and Magic: The Reconstruction of Reality argues for a completely different conception of the structure of reality. Barry Schwartz is an American psychologist and the Dorwin Cartwright Emeritus Professor of Social Theory and Social Action at Swarthmore College. He is author of several famous books including Why We Work and The Paradox of Choice. He argues for a moderated and balanced approach to life. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
subtitle: Is it a mistake to pursue short-term pleasure?

title: Cracking the code for thought
description: Neuroscience has long treated the brain like a computer, despite it being biological, adaptive, and conscious. Max Tegmark, Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski, and Roger Penrose debate whether it is a mistake to see the mind as a complex machine.
filename: HTLGI2025_L58 Cracking the code for thought.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He is best known for his work on general relativity and black holes, and for his public appearances popularising physics and philosophy. Max Tegmark is a Swedish‑American MIT physicist and cosmologist, and president and co-founder of the Future of Life Institute. He is known for championing the Mathematical Universe Hypothesis and pioneering the notion of consciousness as a state of matter. Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski is a theoretical physicist at the Perimeter Institute whose work on space, time, and gravity has been cited by Stephen Hawking. She now leads efforts to encode the universe as a hologram, a bold step toward uniting quantum theory with general relativity.
subtitle: Could consciousness be computational?

title: The strange search for knowledge in the age of post-truth, with Steve Fuller
description: Rather than a linear march toward truth led by experts, Fuller portrays knowledge as contingent and communal. Post-truth, he argues, exposes how media, education and AI actively shape what we know.
speaker_desc: Steve Fuller is Professor of Sociology at the University of Warwick, and a founding figure in the field of social epistemology. He has authored dozens of books, including Post-Truth: Knowledge as a Power Game .

title: Psychoanalysis reveals the unconscious effects of capitalism, with Alenka Zupancic
description: Zupančič argues that despite being well aware of unpleasant truths about the world, our mass psychology is increasingly indifferent towards political action, leaving us vulnerable to new crises.
speaker_desc: Alenka Zupančič is a Slovenian philosopher whose work focuses on psychoanalysis and continental philosophy. A prominent member of the Ljubljana School of Psychoanalysis, Zupančič is best known for her rigorous and often provocative readings of Freud and Lacan, filtered through the lens of German Idealism and Nietzsche.

title: After postmodernism
description:
"Hugely influential in the latter decades of the 20th century, postmodernism transformed many academic disciplines and culture at large. Associated with an attack on objective truth and the uniqueness of meaning, it called into question the whole edifice of knowledge which Western culture had previously glorified. But it left many lost, and in the wake of a polarising post-truth world, there is a widespread recognition that we need to move on. Feminist and post-colonial critics though claim there is a danger that instead we risk retreating to the questionable certainties of the past. Alongside defenders of objective truth like Richard Dawkins and Noam Chomsky, figures like Jordan Peterson argue for a return to moral certainties and belief in the existence of God.  

Are there viable alternatives to postmodernism that are not simply a return to belief in universal truth? Are metamodernism or model-theoretic realism possible ways forward? Or is the chaos initiated by postmodernism so profound that the only credible approach is to return to the Enlightenment notion that we can arrive at the objective truth?"
speaker_desc: Robin van den Akker is Senior Lecturer in the Philosophy of Culture. He is a leading scholar of Metamodernism and founding editor of Notes on Metamodernism. Abby Innes is an Associate Professor in Political Economy at the LSE. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory 'Closure', a post-analytic return to metaphysics, and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism.
subtitle: Escaping certainty and chaos

title: Reason, replication and reality with John Ioannidis
description:
In 2005, John Ioannidis published an essay titled "Why Most Published Research Findings Are False," now the most accessed article in the history of the Public Library of Science.
