title: Paterson Joseph on acting, race, and identity
description: In this inteview, Paterson Joseph discusses his career in acting and the lessons he learned about race, identity, and belonging – lessons which proved invaluable in the writing of his acclaimed book The Secret Diaries of Charles Ignatius Sancho.
speaker_desc: Beginning his career as a Shakespearean actor, Joseph later transitioned to TV with appearances in Casualty and Law and Order, alongside a successful film career. He is the author of The Secret Diaries of Charles Ignatius Sancho, a novel which brilliantly conveys the life and times of the 18th-century composer through fictionalised diaries, letters, and commentary. He is also Chancellor of Oxford Brookes University which has cemented his status as both an actor and public intellectual.
subtitle: Making sense of ourselves

title: Beyond the reality illusion
description: Explore Hilary Lawson's critique of philosophical realism and discover a radical alternative that challenges our understanding of reality and scientific success.
speaker_desc: A British philosopher best known for his theory of 'Closure', Hilary Lawson is an outspoken critic of philosophical realism and Editorial Director of the IAI.
subtitle: Science and the end of the real

title: Ode to outsiders
description: Join Yale Law Professor Amy Chua as she delves into her controversial views on parenting and politics, revealing how rejection can lead to unexpected blessings in her work.
speaker_desc: Best-selling author, former law associate and award-winning academic, Amy Chua is the John M. Duff Jr Professor of Law at Yale Law School where she specialises in topics ranging from ethnic conflict, globalisation and international business transactions. Chua has been named one of Atlantic Monthly’s Brave Thinkers, one of Foreign Policy’s Global Thinkers and has been named one of TIME’s 100 most influential people.
subtitle: How immigrants change the world

title: Truth, theory and ultimate reality
description: We assume our theories are successful because they uncover the true character of reality.  But critics argue there is a danger this is an illusion. Cutting-edge philosopher of physics Tim Maudlin, leading theoretical physicist Lisa Randall, insightful interdisciplinary thinker Abby Innes, and dark-matter physicist Bernard Carr, lock horns over whether theories are true or just our best guesses.
filename: HTLGI2024_H142 Truth, theory and ultiamte reality.HD.downsized.mp4
speaker_desc: Cutting-edge philosopher of physics Tim Maudlin, leading theoretical physicist Lisa Randall, insightful interdisciplinary thinker Abby Innes, and dark-matter physicist Bernard Carr, lock horns over whether theories are true or just our best guesses.
subtitle: Can science ever be true?

title: Destiny: Are we really in control?
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2024_H259 Destiny - are we really in control.fixed.HD.mp4
description: Join ACFM podcast hosts Nadia Idle, Jeremy Gilbert and Keir Milburn for a lively discussion on the social, historical, structural, and psychological, forces that shape us and our fates.
filename: HTLGI2024_H259 Destiny - are we really in control.fixed.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Nadia Idle is a communications lecturer, intellectual and life-long activist from London and Cairo. She runs consciousness-raising workshops to fight atomisation and build collectivity, Jeremy Gilbert is Professor of Cultural and Political Theory at the University of East London, and the current editor of the journal New Formations. Keir Milburn is a writer, researcher and political activist.
subtitle: How society shapes us

title: How moral laws fail feminism
description: In this in-depth interview, Carol Gilligan delves into the biggest studies she conducted throughout her decades-long career as a psychologist — the very same studies with which she shook-up and upended the patriarchal frameworks of the discipline itself.
speaker_desc: Carol Gilligan is an ethicist, psychologist and Professor of Humanities and Applied Psychology at New York University. She is a feminist icon, and the mind behind the revolutionary "ethics of care". She is best known for her now classic work In a Different Voice.
subtitle: An interview with Carol Gilligan

title: The truth about quantum computing
description: There is a tsunami of hype about what quantum computers are going to revolutionise. Join leading quantum computing specialist Scott Aaronson as he challenges the hype and tells us what is really going on.
speaker_desc: Scott Aaronson is one of the top quantum complexity theorists in the world, renowned for both his research in quantum computing and computational complexity theory. Aaronson is famous for his popular blog Shtetl Optimized, which has kept the scientific community up to date on quantum hype for nearly the past two decades. His research and popular writing have earned him numerous awards, including the United States Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers and the Alan T. Waterman Award. Aaronson is an Associate Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at MIT, but took leave of his academic commitments in 2022 to work at OpenAI.
subtitle: Beyond the hype

title: Tyranny of the pen
description: "If you want to change the world, pick up your pen and write," declared Martin Luther King. Watch this video debate on the future of writing with Ruth Padel, John Ralston Saul, and Joanna Kavenna, hosted by Rana Mitter
filename: HTLGI2024_H15 The tyranny of the pen.HD2.mp4
speaker_desc: Rana Mitter hosts this debate on the future of writing, whether its era has passed or if its cultural influence remains. Joining him for this panel are Ruth Padel, an award-winning poet, novelist and non-fiction writer, John Ralston Saul, an essayist, novelist and the former President of PEN International, and, finally, the acclaimed novelist and writer Jo Kavenna, who in 2013 was named as one of Granta’s Best Young British Novelists.
subtitle: Is the age of the pen over?

title: How to win against power and privilege
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2023_L57 How to win against power and privilege.HD.mp4
description: Too often the legal system feels like it only works for people who already have power. But times are changing. Join leading barrister, Jolyon Maugham KC, as he identifies how the law can also put power in the hands of ordinary people.
filename: HTLGI2023_L57 How to win against power and privilege.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Jolyon Maugham KC is an activist barrister, founder of the Good Law Project, and thorn in the side of the government. Jolyon is most famous for his use of the law to hold the government to account. Through the Good Law Project, Jolyon has sought to challenge the UK government's approach to Brexit, Covid, and transgender rights. From humble origins to a foremost legal force, Jolyon has become a key defence against government overreach.
subtitle: Rethinking our legal system

title: Nancy Sherman on stoicism and society
description: Stoicism has become increasingly popular on social media but are people missing the point? Join Nancy Sherman as she sets the record straight on Stoicism and argues for its importance in our everyday lives.
speaker_desc: Nancy Sherman is Professor of Philosophy at Georgetown University and a New York Times Notable Author. Her latest book is Stoic Wisdom: Ancient Lessons for Modern Resilience. She is also the author of Afterwar: Healing the Moral Wounds of our Soldiers, among various other book on ethics, drawing especially from the ancients and her experience as the inaugural Distinguished Chair in Ethics at the United States Naval Academy.
subtitle: Ancient philosophies for modern problems

title: The agents of life
description: Should we move away from a biology of organisms, and recognise the interconnected character of life? Join Denis Noble, Frances Ashcroft and Johnjoe McFaddem as they debate the true nature of life.
speaker_desc: Oxford biologist Denis Noble, pioneering researcher and geneticist Frances Ashcroft, and multidisciplinary scientist Johnjoe McFadden, debate life and its environment. Shini Somara hosts.
subtitle: Should we abandon the idea of individual organisms

title: The new overlords
description: Will free-market capitalism always lead to monopolies without regulation? Join former President of Armenia Armen Sarkissian, the former Finance Minister for Iraq Ali Allawi and co-founder of the Institute for Journalism and Social Change Claire Provost as they debate the future of our economies.
speaker_desc: Armen Sarkissian is the former President of Armenia, a physicist, investor, businessman and computer scientist. He spearheaded Armenia’s response to the 'Velvet Revolution' and border skirmishes with Azerbaijan. Claire Provost is an investigative journalist and co-founder and co-director of the non-profit Institute for Journalism and Social Change specialising in the backroom dealings of the largest corporations. Ali Allawi served as Deputy Prime Minister, Finance Minister and Minister of Defence of Iraq. He has also worked as a Professor at the University of Oxford, and a visiting Fellow at Harvard.
subtitle: Can we defeat monopolies?

title: The devil in all of us
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2024_H155 The devil in all of us.HD.mp4
description: Many have had the experience of an urge to do something wrong just for the hell of it. Join Yale psychologist Paul Bloom as he invites us to see the clever, creative and beautiful side of our impulses toward evil.
filename: HTLGI2024_H155 The devil in all of us.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Paul Bloom is a trailblazing Canadian American psychologist, bestselling author and celebrated speaker. He is the Brooks and Suzanne Ragen Professor Emeritus of psychology and cognitive science at Yale University and Professor of Psychology at the University of Toronto.
subtitle: Our human shadow

title: Avshalom Elitzur on physics, consciousness, and politics
description: Physicist-philosopher Avshalom Elitzur believes that panpsychism provides the most promising explanation of consciousness. Join Elitzur for a wide-ranging discussion covering quantum physics, consciousness, time, environmentalism, and the Israel-Palestine conflict.
speaker_desc: Avshalom Elitzur is a Professor in the Centre for Quantum Studies at Chapman University in the United States and is deemed by many to be an intellectual powerhouse in both the fields of physics and philosophy. Having left school at sixteen to work as a lab technician, he presented a paper on quantum mechanics at Temple University, after which he was invited to Tel Aviv University to complete his doctorate on the subject. Elitzur is best known for his work on the Elitzur–Vaidman bomb-testing problem in quantum mechanics.
subtitle: Mind, matter and beyond

title: Rationality in the dock
description: Rationality has often been cited as a key factor in the uncovering of truth. But today, in a world of competing and often radically incompatible perspectives, reason has been called into question and rationality is seen as a rhetorical strategy to defend outdated views.
speaker_desc: Kathleen Stock is a daring and bold philosopher famous for her gender-critical views. She is a founding faculty fellow at the University of Austin. Carol Gilligan is a groundbreaking feminist, ethicist and psychologist based at New York University. Michael Shermer is the founder of The Skeptics Society. He is best known for his searing critiques of pseudoscience and the supernatural. Myriam François hosts.
subtitle: Life at the end of reason

title: The price of life
description: We say that life is priceless. Right? So why do so many people put a value on human life as part of their job. Join journalist and broadcaster, Jenny Kleeman in this engaging talk..
speaker_desc: Jenny Kleeman is a distinguished British journalist, broadcaster and author. After two decades at the cutting edge of politics and culture, Kleeman boasts an impressive career spanning foreign correspondence, radio hosting, and presenting for the BBC, Channel 4 and HBO.
subtitle: Who decides what we're worth?

title: The laws of physics are not fixed
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2024_H13 The laws of physics are not fixed.HD.mp4
description: Join pioneering physicist, João Magueijo, as he argues that everything we thought we knew about the laws of physics is wrong. They do change. And they can be violated. What's more, a new understanding of these laws could help solve the mystery of dark matter.
filename: HTLGI2024_H13 The laws of physics are not fixed.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: João Magueijo is a Portuguese cosmologist and professor in theoretical physics at Imperial College London. He is a pioneer of the varying speed of light (VSL) theory.
subtitle: A radical new path for physics and reality

title: Yale's 'Tiger Mom' on tribalism today
description: The world is divided into tribes - religions, nationalities and political parties, to list just a few. But how important are these tribal differences in international affairs? Join Yale Proffesor and self-proclaimed 'Tiger Mom' Amy Chua in this exclusive interview to find out.
speaker_desc: Amy Chua is the John M. Duff Jr Professor of Law at Yale Law School where she specialises in ethnic conflict, globalisation and international business transactions. Alongside her best-selling parenting memoir, Battle Hymn of the Tiger Mother, Chua has written for major publications on the state of American politics, tribalism, identity politics, polarization and nationalism. Most recently, she was awarded the Lux and Veritas Prize by the Buckley Institute for fostering intellectual diversity in her classroom and beyond.
subtitle: Understanding a divided world

title: The great rewiring of our lives
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/IAILIVE2024_47 The great rewiring of our lives.HD.downsized.mp4
description: 'Since the arrival of social media anxiety has increased by 92% for those between 18-25. Join Jonathan Haidt, Katherine Birbalsingh, and Emily Edlynn as they debate what can be done about the anxious generation.
filename: IAILIVE2024_47 The great rewiring of our lives.HD.downsized.mp4
speaker_desc: Jonathan Haidt, a renowned psychologist and NYU Stern professor, has made significant contributions to moral psychology. His latest book, The Anxious Generation, attributes teen mental distress to reduced free play and increased smartphone use. Katharine Birbalsingh CBE, 'Britain's strictest headmistress,' founded Michaela Community School in 2014, securing the country's top Progress 8 score. Emily Edlynn, PhD is a clinical psychologist passionate about integrating science and common-sense in parenting guidance to support healthier and more sustainable lives for parents. She is an award-winning author of the book, Autonomy-Supportive Parenting
subtitle: Have we ruined childhood forever?

title: Better left unsaid
description: Unexpressed emotions never die... but are buried alive and come forth later in uglier ways' claimed Sigmund Freud. Cultural critic Theodore Dalrymple,  psychiatrist Simon Wessely, and positive psychology specialist Vanessa King debate whether Freud was dangerously wrong and if saying nothing is better than saying anything at all.
speaker_desc: Theodore Dalrymple is the pen-name for Anthony Malcolm Daniels, an English cultural critic, prolific writer, satirist, prison physician and psychiatrist. Vanessa King is a positive psychology expert and a board member at Action for Happiness. Simon Wessely is the Regius Professor of Psychiatry at King's College London and Former president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists. Our host Peter York is a columnist, broadcaster, management consultant, and author of 1982's The Sloane Ranger Handbook.
subtitle: Our unexpressed emotions

title: Conflict and its future
description: General Petraeus has been at the forefront of international affairs for many decades, and holds strong views on recent US foreign policy. In a world more precarious than ever, join him to hear his assessment of how to respond to the challenges of contemporary global affairs, and gain insight into how his own life experiences influenced his philosophy on leadership.
speaker_desc: General (U.S. Army, Ret.) David H. Petraeus is the Kissinger Fellow at Yale’s Jackson School of Global Affairs, the Chair of the Global Institute of a major investment firm, and a former director of the CIA. Petraeus served over 37 years in the U.S. military, culminating his career with six consecutive commands as a general officer, five of which were in combat, including command of the Surge in Iraq, command of U.S. Central Command, and command of coalition forces in Afghanistan. Following retirement from the military, Petraeus served as Director of the CIA during the global war on terror. He is the author, with Andrew Roberts, of Conflict: A Military History of the Evolution of Warfare from 1945 to Ukraine. Petraeus graduated with honors from the U.S. Military Academy and earned a Ph.D. at Princeton University.
subtitle: Strategic leadership in action

title: The tech crisis
description: We are entering into an increasingly difficult period for freedom of expression because the technologies we hoped would support freedom turn out to pose a threat to it. Join the political philosopher Time magazine labelled a 'prophet' of anti-globalism, John Ralston Saul, as he argues that globalist ideology harms freedom of speech.
speaker_desc: John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and President Emeritus of PEN International. His 16 works, including Voltaire’s Bastards and The Collapse of Globalism, have been translated into 29 languages in 38 countries. He has been recognised internationally with a host of literary awards, including Chile’s Pablo Neruda Medal, South Korea’s Manhae Grand Prize for Literature, Italy’s Premio Letterario Internazionale and Canada’s Governor General’s Literary Award for Non-fiction.
subtitle: Humanity's response to tech and globalisation

title: Consciousness pre-dates life
description: Many scientists, operating with a materialist worldview, argue that consciousness emerges out of inanimate molecules. In contrast, Roger Penrose's long-time collaborator, Stuart Hameroff, puts forward the controversial case that consciousness precedes life.
speaker_desc: Stuart Hameroff is an American anesthesiologist and professor at the University of Arizona known for his studies of consciousness and his controversial claim, alongside Sir Roger Penrose, that consciousness originates from quantum states in neural microtubules.
subtitle: New evidence for a radical theory

title: Land, ownership and hypocrisy
description: Since Magna Carta, we assume individuals have a right to the property or land that they own. If nations, like Ukraine, are invaded we champion their right to retrieve their land. But there is a risk these principles which we think universal are only applied to the strong.
speaker_desc: Peter Singer is one of the most prominent figures in contemporary ethics. He has been recognized with numerous accolades, including the Berggruen Prize and, most recently, the BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Awards. Dale Turner is an Associate Professor in the Department of Political Science and Centre for Indigenous Studies at the University of Toronto. He is working on his first hotly-anticipated novel, Vision, which draws from postcolonial and indigenous thought. Tommy J. Curry holds a Personal Chair in Africana philosophy and Black Male studies at the University of Edinburgh. In 2018, he won an American Book Award for the The Man-Not: Race, Class, Genre, and the Dilemmas of Black Manhood. Janne Teller is a critically-acclaimed writer of novels, essays, and short stories. Teller has received many literary awards including the Drassow’s Prize for literary works towards peace and human understanding. Hosted by Barry C. Smith.
subtitle: How to deal with native land

title: In defence of privacy
description: The Leveson Inquiry raised questions about the conduct of the press but also reignited a deeper debate regarding freedom and privacy. Join star celebrity Hugh Tomlinson KC as he argues for the essential right of privacy.
speaker_desc: Hugh Tomlinson KC is an English barrister and translator of the philosopher Gilles Deleuze. He is a noted specialist in media and information law including defamation, confidence, privacy and data protection. Tomlinson is famed for the central role he played in the litigation that sought the full disclosure of UK MP’s parliamentary expenses and was also a key figure in the News of The World phone-hacking case.
subtitle: A worthy trade for freedom

title: The future of particle physics
description: The more we understand the world, the more it seems to unravel into larger and more complex mysteries that may well be unsolvable. Join Cambridge particle physicist and CERN hadron collider researcher, Harry Cliff, to explore the fascinating anomalies and oddities that confound scientists.
filename: HTLGI2024_H143 The future of particle physics.HD.downsized..mp4
speaker_desc: Harry Cliff is a particle physicist at the University of Cambridge and carries out research with the LHCb experiment at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider. He was a curator at the Science Museum, London for seven years and regularly gives public lectures and makes TV and radio appearances.
subtitle: The final science

title: The real me
description: Many identify themselves with their inner voice - the silent voice we use to think, plan, and ponder. But from Lacan to Nietzsche, psychologists and philospohers have warned this inner voice is not the self, nor is it innocent or harmless.
speaker_desc: Steve Taylor is a senior lecturer in psychology at Leeds Beckett University and author of several best-selling books in the fields of psychology and spirituality. Jack Symes is a public philosopher, writer, and researcher at Durham University. Anneli Jefferson is a philosopher of psychology and moral philosophy, and lecturer at Cardiff University. And Frank Tallis is a clinical psychologist who specialises in obsessive compulsive disorder. Hosted by novelist Joanna Kavenna.
subtitle: Understanding our inner voices

title: Nightmare in suburbia
description: The classic picture of success for much of the last century has been a detached suburban house, 2.4 kids, and a shiny car. But is there a danger this dream of domestic bliss is out of touch with the reality.
speaker_desc: Mary Ann Sieghart hosts a debate on whether we need to abandon the nuclear family for a more communal model of living, or the family structures we're used to have withstood the test of time for a reason. Joining her are Nadia Idle, a communications lecturer and co-host of the left-wing podcast ACFM, Des Fitzgerald, a professor of Medical Humanities and Social Sciences at UCC, and Hannah Rich, a Senior Researcher at Theos. This event was sponsored by Theos.
subtitle: The myth of the nuclear family

title: The trouble with language
description: For centuries we imagined that language was transparent. The 20th century changed all that. Philosophy, with the so-called linguistic turn, came to see language as central to our understanding of reality and set out to make it precise.
speaker_desc: Hilary Lawson is a post-postmodern philosopher and a renowned critic of philosophical realism. He is best known for his work on reflexivity and his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist metaphysics arguing that we close the openness of the world with our thought and language. Tim Maudlin is Professor of Philosophy at NYU and Founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics. In his ground-breaking book The Metaphysics Within Physics, Truth and Paradox: Solving the Riddles and Quantum Non-Locality and Relativity, Maudlin challenges Einstein's criticisms of Quantum Mechanics as 'spooky action at a distance'. Maudlin is one of the world’s leading philosophical realists.
subtitle: Does language describe reality?

title: Scott Aaronson on consciousness and AI safety
description: AI and ChatGPT have made extraordinary progress in recent years. But what are we to make of such progress? In this interview, world-renowned quantum computing expert Scott Aaronson discusses AI safety, quantum mechanics, and what makes human experience unique.
speaker_desc: Scott Aaronson is one of the top quantum complexity theorists in the world, renowned for both his research in quantum computing and computational complexity theory. Aaronson is famous for his popular blog Shtetl Optimized, which has kept the scientific community up to date on quantum hype for nearly the past two decades.
subtitle: The future of artificial intelligence

title: Neoliberalism: A Soviet nightmare
description: Professor Abby Innes argues that the utopianism that guided the Soviet Union to disaster is eerily similar to the decline of our modern politics, and for Western states to succeed they need to throw off the shackles of utopianism and rediscover the scientific method.
speaker_desc: Dr Abby Innes weaves political analysis with the scientific method to expose the ironic similarities between our current politics and the Soviet Union. She is an Associate Professor of Political Economy at the European Institute at the LSE. Her work focuses on party-state development, the transition from the Soviet system in Eastern Europe and the modern neoliberal state.
subtitle: Soviet and neoliberal false utopianism

title: Navigating the new world order
description: Delve into the shifting landscape of international relations, from rising tensions in Europe to regional conflicts in the Middle East and South China Sea. Can international cooperation and treaties ensure our safety, or is global dominance the only solution?
filename: H24_141 Navigating the new world order.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Christina Lamb OBE is the Chief Foreign Correspondent for the Times and Sunday Times, bestselling author and honorary fellow of University College Oxford. Armen Sarkissian is the former President of Armenia, a physicist, investor, businessman and computer scientist. And Bronwen Maddox is the Director and Chief Executive of Chatham House. Before joining Chatham House, Bronwen was Director of the Institute for Government, and she served as the chief foreign commentator, foreign editor and US editor at The Times. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
subtitle: The new world disorder

title: Exposing the Windrush scandal
description: The role of journalism is to speak truth to power and no story embodies this better than the Windrush Scandal. Join award-winning journalist Amelia Gentleman as she discusses the values of investigative journalism and reveals how she exposed the biggest political scandal of the decade.
speaker_desc: Amelia Gentleman is an acclaimed British journalist, Guardian reporter and author of 'The Windrush Betrayal: Exposing the hostile Environment', which was a New Statesman and Spectator book of the year, shortlisted for the Orwell Prize for Political Writing and longlisted for Bailee Gifford prize.
subtitle: Journalism’s impact on political scandals

title: Belief, value and superstition
description: Prominent psychologists, critics and authors debate the rise in new age and traditional religious belief in the young. Is it a dangerous return of unsupported fantasy, and a threat to rationalism, or rather a welcome sign of a desire for an agreed moral framework in response to the chaos of a post-truth world?
speaker_desc: Winston Marshall is a podcaster and political/cultural commentator, writing for publications such as The Spectator. He was previously member and is co-founder of the famous folk rock band Mumford & Sons. Paul Bloom is a psychologist and professor at Yale University and the University of Toronto. He has written about empathy, pleasure and suffering, for example in his book Against Empathy: The Case for Rational Compassion. Janne Teller is a novellist whose works have sold millions of copies. Her 2010 novel Nothing received numerous awards. Fellipe do Vale is the assistant professor of biblical and systematic theology at Trinity Evangelical Divinity School in Illinois. His research focuses on the connection between moral theology and theological anthropology. Rana Mitter hosts.
subtitle: Are we entering a new age of belief?

title: AI and the creativity crisis
description: Creativity is often seen as a uniquely human quality. But with generative AI competing with and rivalling human skills, is this core facet of humanity under threat? Join Judith Donath, Martha Fiennes and John Ralston Saul as they debate the effect AI will have on art.
filename: HTLGI2024_H57 AI and the creativity crisis.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Judith Donath is a social media expert and fellow at Harvard's Berkman Center, as well as the founder of the Social Media Group at the MIT Media Lab. Martha Fiennes is an award-winning film director, writer and producer, best known for her films Onegin and Chromophobia. John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and a long-time champion of freedom of expression. He has written numerous best-selling books on culture, politics and philosophy. Hosted by Niki Seth Smith and sponsored by The New Humanist.
subtitle: Are we seeing the end of human made art?

title: Genes are not the blueprint for life
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2024_H164 Genes are not the blueprint for life.HD.mp4
description: Join renowned Oxford biologist, Denis Noble, as he proposes the radical new theory that organisms control their genomes rather than the other way around.
filename: HTLGI2024_H164 Genes are not the blueprint for life.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Denis Noble is Professor Emeritus and co-Director of Computational Physiology at Oxford University. Noble was one of the pioneers of Systems Biology and developed the first viable mathematical model of the working heart. His books include the first popular science book on the subject, The Music of Life, which has been translated into 12 languages.
subtitle: Going beyond the selfish gene

title: The puzzle of perception with Barry C. Smith
description: Join Barry Smith in this interview as he  describes how philosophy has ignored the senses fail to understand their complexity, their role in our everyday lives and their impact on our consciousness and reality.
subtitle: How our senses affect our reality

title: Truth, Gaza, and reportage
description: Truth, it is sometimes said, is the first casualty of war. And the terrible events in Gaza are seemingly no exception. But what should our strategy be when seeking to understand what is happening on the ground? Is there a simple fact of the matter which we can uncover?
filename: HTLGI2024_H24_80 Telling the story of war.HD..downsized..mp4
speaker_desc: Sophie Scott-Brown is joined by Myriam François, an author, broadcaster and academic on issues related to Islam, France and the Middle East, and Uriel Abulof, Professor of Political Science at Tel Aviv University and author of The Mortality and Morality of Nations, to examine whether we can overcome the limitations of truth in times of war.
subtitle: Telling the story of war

title: Mystery in the making
description: Can science really give us all the answers? Join Harry Cliff, Claudia de Rham and Avshalom Elitzur as they debate the efficacy of science as a guide to reality.
speaker_desc: Theoretical physicists Claudia de Rham and Avshalom Elitzur debate the mysteries of the universe with experimental CERN physicist Harry Cliff.
subtitle: Does science provide a complete explanation?

title: Stoicism reimagined
description: We think that stoicism is defined by a rugged self-reliance and indifference to events. Join  philosopher, Nancy Sherman, as she argues this is mistaken, and that building deep emotional connections is as important for stoics as it is for everyone else.
speaker_desc: Nancy Sherman is a Professor of Philosophy at Georgetown University who has conducted research in general ethics, moral psychology and the history of philosophy with a focus on the stoic tradition. She is a New York Times Notable Author and, from 1997-1999, served as the inaugural Distinguished Chair in Ethics at the U.S. Naval Academy.
subtitle: Nancy Sherman on ancient wisdom for a modern world

title: Jessica DeFino on the politics of beauty
description: Jessica De Fino is an award-winning beauty reporter and critic. Join her as she discusses what beauty really means, why we need to divest from the beauty industry and how we should divert from the toxic beauty standards perpetuated by the industry.
speaker_desc: Jessica De Fino is an award-winning beauty reporter and critic (New York Times, Sunday Times, Vice). She writes the beauty advice column Ask Ugly and publishes a weekly newsletter The Review of Beauty which “basically gives the middle finger to the entire beauty industry” (HuffPost).
subtitle: Why the beauty industry needs a revamp

title: The future of politics
description: John Bercow was once seen as on the right of the Tory party, later becoming a member of the Tory shadow cabinet. He moved to the left throughout his political career subsequently becoming a thorn in the side of the Conservative Johnson government. Join him as he outlines his vision for the future and why Britain desperately needs change.
speaker_desc: John Bercow is one of the most recognisable and iconoclastic figures in British politics. As Speaker of the House of Commons from 2009 to 2019, his distinctive bellow for order spanned the tenure of four Prime Ministers and a decade of political turmoil.
subtitle: Finding order amongst the chaos

title: Singles, sex and society
description: The rise in singles, now over 40%, sparks debate: Is it a societal threat due to lower birth rates, or a positive shift for personal lives and population control?
speaker_desc: Güneş Taylor hosts a debate on the changing face of relationships, the increasing number of singles in our society and whether marriage has become obsolete. She is joined by Yasmin Benoit, an asexual activist, model and writer, Edward Davies, the Policy Director of the Centre of Social Justice, and Aline Laurent-Mayard, a journalist, author and podcast host.
subtitle: Is marriage finally obsolete?

title: Reality after realism
description: Join renegade analytic philosopher Michael Della Rocca and post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson as they put realism to the test and propose radically different solutions for understanding of both language and the world.
speaker_desc: Michael Della Rocca is a leading authority on Spinoza and expert in early modern philosophy. He is Sterling Professor of Philosophy at Yale University. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and editorial director of the Institute of Art and Ideas. His main work, Closure: a story of Everything, has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Renowned intellectual historian Sophie Scott-Brown hosts.
subtitle: Embracing the death of language

title: Tasneem Husain on creativity in physics
description: Join theoretical physicist Tasneem Husain for an in-depth interview on her path to theoretical physics. From the puzzles of physics that first drew her to the discipline, physics' need for more creative minds, and the importance of being scientifically literate in our increasingly technological world.
speaker_desc: Tasneem Zehra Husain is a theoretical physicist, writer, and educator. She is one of few Pakistani women to obtain a doctorate in physics, and the first Pakistani woman string theorist. Only the Longest Threads is her debut novel.
subtitle: Why we need more creative minds in science

title: Why we fail to predict market crashes
description: There is very little that is certain in economics and we always know that the next devastating financial crisis could be just around the corner. Join LSE and Oxford economist, Linda Yueh, to explore how we can predict and contain the next financial crash.
speaker_desc: Economist and former BBC Chief Business correspondent Professor Linda Yueh holds positions as Fellow of Economics at St Edmunds College, Oxford, as well as Adjunct Professor of Economics at London Business School.
subtitle: Learning lessons from the history of finance

title: Violence, vengeance and virtue
description: What is the relationship between morality and ppression? Are violence and vengeance no more acceptable on the part of the victim than the aggressor? Or is morality inextricably linked to the circumstances of the actors? Join Peter Singer, Ghada Karmi, and Uriel Abulof in this video debate to find out. Hosted by Mary Ann Seighart
speaker_desc: Peter Singer is one of the most prominent figures in contemporary ethics. He is an Australian moral philosopher and the Emeritus Ira W. DeCamp Professor of Bioethics at Princeton University and the author of Animal Liberation. Ghada Karmi is a Palestinian-born academic, physician and author. She held a number of research appointments on Middle Eastern politics and culture at the School of Oriental and African Studies, and in the Universities of Durham and Leeds. Uriel Abulof is an associate professor at Tel-Aviv University’s School of Political Science, Government and International Affairs. Mary Ann Seighart hosts.
subtitle: The relationship between violence and ethics

title: The life and philosophy of Paterson Joseph
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2024_H173 The life and philosophy of Paterson Joseph.HD_1.mp4
description: The ability to inhabit a character, especially one underappreciated and consigned to the annuls of history, is both fiendishly difficult and personally revealing. Join Wonka, Peep Show and Shakespearean actor, Paterson Joseph, as he reveals the key experiences that led him to his personal philosophy and outlook on life.
filename: HTLGI2024_H173 The life and philosophy of Paterson Joseph.HD_1.mp4
speaker_desc: Paterson Joseph is a cultural icon, best known for his roles in TV and film, from 'Peep Show' to 'Wonka', and his career in theatre with the Royal Shakespeare Company. He is also the current Chancellor of Oxford Brookes University. Jenny Kleeman hosts.
subtitle: Acting, performance, and identity

title: General David Petraeus on Ukraine, Israel and the future of war
description: Join former CIA director General David Petraeus in this insightful interview on US foreign policy shapes the world of conflict we live in today.
speaker_desc: General (U.S. Army, Ret.) David H. Petraeus is the Kissinger Fellow at Yale’s Jackson School of Global Affairs, and a former director of the CIA. Petraeus served over 37 years in the U.S. military, culminating his career with six consecutive commands as a general officer, five of which were in combat, including command of the Surge in Iraq, command of U.S. Central Command, and command of coalition forces in Afghanistan. This interview was recorded on Sunday 26th May 2024, at HowTheLightGetsIn, Hay-on-Wye.
subtitle: What the world can learn from US foreign policy

title: AI and the end of humanity
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/IAILIVE2024_46 AI and the end of humanity.HD.downsized.mp4
description: Does AI fundamentally challenge what it means to be human? Join Eliezer Yudkowsky, Scott Aaronson, Liv Boeree and Joscha Bach in this thought-provoking video debate to learn more.
filename: IAILIVE2024_46 AI and the end of humanity.HD.downsized.mp4
speaker_desc: Eliezer Yudkowsky is a leading AI safety researcher, renowned for popularizing the concept of friendly AI. Scott Aaronson is one of the top quantum complexity theorists in the world, renowned for both his research in quantum computing and computational complexity theory. A self-confessed nerd with a first-class degree in astrophysics, Liv Boeree combined her science background and passion for games to become one of the most recognizable faces in professional poker. Joscha Bach is a cognitive scientist who is pushing the limits of what we can achieve with Artificial Intelligence. Güneş Taylor hosts.
subtitle: Does AI change what it means to be human?

title: The Indian Century
description: The world's largest democracy, India, is seen as the West's obvious ally against the growing might of China. But is that really the case? Find out more in this engaging debate.
speaker_desc: S.Y. Quraishi is an Indian civil servant who rose to be the 17th Chief Election Commissioner of India. Kate Sullivan de Estrada is the Director of the Contemporary South Asian Studies Programme and Associate Professor in the International Relations of South Asia. Alpa Shah is a Professor of Anthropology at the London School of Economics, specialising in Indian and Nepalese minority and indigenous groups. Hosted by Rana Mitter, Harvard University ST Lee Chair in US-Asia Relations.
subtitle: Does India need the West?

title: Ruby Wax on mental health in a mad world
description: Join multifaceted comedian and author Ruby Wax in an in-depth interview on the search for meaning, the pitfalls of fame, and her own experiences with depression.
speaker_desc: Mental health, depression, comedy. Ruby Wax OBE is a seminal British-American talent, excelling as an actress, writer, TV personality, and mental health advocate. Her latest book is I Am Not As Well As I Thought I Was.
subtitle: Finding meaning in the madness

title: How oceans shaped the world
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2023_H181 How the ocean shaped the world.HD.mp4
description: Join leading oceanographer and broadcaster, Helen Czerski, as she argues that the ocean is not merely a feature of our planet, but an extraordinary engine on which we all depend - a phenomenal blue machine.
filename: HTLGI2023_H181 How the ocean shaped the world.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Dr Helen Czerski is a a physicist, oceanographer, presenter and author, currently working as an Associate Professor at University College London in the Department of Mechanical Engineering.
subtitle: Saving the heart of our planet

title: Nihilism and the meaning of life
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2023_L90 Nihilism and the meaning of life.HD.mp4
description: Nihilism, the abandonment of all fundamental beliefs, may appear a hopeless outlook. Yet perhaps it also has potential.  Join Dutch philosopher, Nolen Gertz, as he makes the case that in our technological age nihilism is unavoidable but with the right response we can live open, worthwhile, prosperous lives.
filename: HTLGI2023_L90 Nihilism and the meaning of life.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Nolen Gertz is Associate Professor of Applied Philosophy at the University of Twente, the Coordinator of the Human Condition Research Line of ESDIT, and a Senior Researcher of the 4TU.Centre for Ethics and Technology. His research focuses primarily on the intersection of political philosophy, existential phenomenology, and philosophy of technology.
subtitle: Losing hope in the information age

title: Is specialisation killing us?
description: Join David Healy, Caitjan Gainty, and Nick Lane analysing the role of medical specialisation within healthcare in this engaging video debate. Hosted by Mark Salter
speaker_desc: David Healy is a psychiatrist, scientist, author and professor of psychiatry at Bangor University in the United Kingdom. Caitjan Gainty is a historian of science and expert on twentieth century health and healthcare. She is a Senior Lecturer in the History of Science, Technology & Medicine at King’s College London. Nick Lane is a British biochemist and outstanding science communicator, asking the difficult question: what is the origin of life? He is a Professor of Evolutionary Biochemistry at University College London and a bestselling author. Hosted by Mark Salter.
subtitle: Life, death, and specialisation

title: How to heal a divided nation
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2023_H250 How to heal a divided nation.HD.downsized.mp4
description: We are more polarised than ever before. On almost every major issue we are split down the middle and then shout across the divide violently. Join rising star author, Grafton Tanner, to question this narrative and explore how to divide a nation and how to put it back together again.
filename: HTLGI2023_H250 How to heal a divided nation.HD.downsized.mp4
speaker_desc: Grafton Tanner is the author of The Hours Have Lost Their Clock: The Politics of Nostalgia with Repeater Books. He also hosts Delusioneering, an audio series about the myths of capitalism, and writes and performs music with his band Superpuppet.
subtitle: We're not as polarised as we think

title: John Vervaeke on the purpose of consciousness
description: Join John Vervaeke in this exclusive studio interview as he argues for a naturalistic account of mystical experience.
speaker_desc: John Vervaeke is an award-winning professor of psychology, cognitive science, and Buddhist psychology at the University of Toronto.
subtitle: Towards a naturalistic account of consciousness

title: A radical step to gender equality
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2023_L43 A radical step towards gender equality.HD.downsized.mp4
description: Is it time to make childbirth a technological, not a biological, phenomenon? Reproductive medicine has made huge strides over the last few decades. Now it is claimed we are within ten years of developing an artificial womb, raising the possibility that having children could take place without pregnancy or childbirth. Are artificial wombs a hope or a threat?
filename: HTLGI2023_L43 A radical step towards gender equality.HD.downsized.mp4
speaker_desc: Join author and ethnographer Kristen Ghodsee, writer and editor Mary Harrington, and transhumanist and researcher Anders Sandberg as they debate the potentials of artificial wombs. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
subtitle: Making childbirth a technical phenomenon

title: Being good and being bad
description: Join Katheleen Stock, Hilary Greaves and Hilary Lawson as they debate the morality of terror and violence when used for supposed good.
filename: HTLGI2023_L134 Being good and being bad.HD.downsized.mp4
subtitle: Morality in the modern world

title: Sleeping with the enemy
description: In our digitally-driven dating scene, with the ability to choose specific characteristics, many avoid dating across the political divide. Join happiness expert Paul Dolan as he argues dating those we disagree with is valuable both for ourselves as individuals and for society.
speaker_desc: Paul Dolan is a Professor in the Department of Social Policy at the London School of Economics and Political Science where he holds a Chair in Behavioural Science.
subtitle: Why we should date those we disagree with

title: Smashing particles at the energy frontier
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/IAILIVE2024_43S Smashing particles on the energy frontier.HD.mp4
description: At CERN's Large Hadron Collider, physicists create the world's highest energy human-made collisions to explore the fundamental building blocks of the universe. Join Yale Professor Sarah Demers as she describes how CERN researchers create, and learn from, these collisions at the energy frontier.
filename: IAILIVE2024_43S Smashing particles on the energy frontier.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Sarah Demers is an American physicist and the Horace D Taft associate professor of physics at Yale University.
subtitle: Discover the building blocks of the universe

title: The reality of living forever
description: Join David Gems, Sunetra Gupta, Nolen Gertz in this exciting video debate questioning our relationship with death and our obsession with living forever.
filename: HTLGI2023_L24 The reality of living forever.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: David Gems is a Professor of Biogerontology at University College London. Sunetra Gupta is a Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford, as well as an acclaimed novelist and essayist. Nolen Gertz is an Assistant Professor of Applied Philosophy at the University of Twente known for his work on nihilism. Güneş Taylor hosts.
subtitle: Should we stop resisting death?

title: Betty Sue Flowers on Myths and Modernity
description: In this interview, Betty Sue Flowers explores how myths and legends still shape contemporary life, from religious stories and heroic tales to the narratives behind our economies.
speaker_desc: Betty Sue Flowers is a writer, editor and international business consultant. She is the former director of the Lyndon Baines Johnson Library and Museum and an Emerita Professor of English at the University of Texas at Austin. She pioneered the modern, psychological appreciation of ancient myths alongside the esteemed Joseph Campbell - whose work was famously the inspiration for the Star Wars franchise.
subtitle: The power of legend

title: Protest, democracy and power
description: Protest is essential to democracy. Protest allows us to fight for justice without resorting to radical forms of conflict or even civil war. But governments are often tempted to give police powers to shut down disruptive protest. Join civil rights campaigner, Peter Tatchell, as he argues that without protest, democracy is lost.
speaker_desc: Peter Tatchell is a human rights campaigner best known for his work with LGBTQ+ movements, a member of the gay rights group Outrage! and director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation, a human rights organization. Peter began campaigning in London, organizing sit-ins at pubs that refused to serve gay people and protests against the classification of homosexuality as an illness.
subtitle: A worthy trade for freedom

title: Astonishment, fear, and quantum physics
description: Join leading philosopher of physics, Tim Maudlin, in this  talk as he makes the case for the importance of Bell's theorem and explores a result physics has been too afraid to confront.
filename: HTLGI2023_L85 Astonishment, fear and quantum physics.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: One of the world's foremost philosophers of physics, Tim Maudlin is Professor of Philosophy at NYU and Founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics.
subtitle: Accepting Bell's theorem

title: Mind, matter, and everything
description: Join physicist Sean Carrol, psychologist Ellen Langer and philosopher Tamar Gendler in this thought-provoking video debate uncovering the true secrets of consciousness and the mind.
speaker_desc: Sean Carroll is the Homewood Professor of Natural Philosophy at John Hopkins University, and Fractal Faculty at the Santa Fe Institute. He also hosts the weekly podcast Mindscape, which explores interesting ideas in science, philosophy, culture, and the arts. Ellen Langer is Professor of Psychology at Harvard University and the author of The Mindful Body. Among other honours, she is the recipient of three distinguished scientist awards, a Guggenheim Fellowship, and the Liberty Science Genius Award. She is widely known as the mother of mindfulness. Tamar Gendler is Yale University's Dean of the Faculty of Arts and Sciences, the Vincent J. Scully Professor of Philosophy, and Professor of Psychology and Cognitive Science. A philosophical powerhouse bringing together the techniques of traditional Anglo-American philosophy with empirical work from psychology and other social sciences. Jack Symes hosts.
subtitle: Can consciousness be solved by science?

title: A universe of possibility
description: The fundamental structure of the cosmos is not atoms, particles, or even thoughts or mind; the fundamental structure of the Universe is possibility. Join one of the world's leading cosmologists and Hawking collaborator, George Ellis, as he argues possibilities underlie our whole physical and mental existence.
speaker_desc: George Ellis is a distinguished professor at the University of Cape Town in South Africa. He co-authored 'The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time' with physicist Stephen Hawking, and is considered one of the world's leading theorists in cosmology.
subtitle: How reality emerges from chance

title: Bill Browder On Surviving Putin
description: Explore the intricate workings of Russia and the significance of understanding Putin's actions amidst the Ukraine war. Discover Bill Browder's journey as Putin's top adversary, surviving assassination attempts and becoming a renowned expert on Russian politics and activism for justice.
speaker_desc: Bill Browder is an American-born British financier and political activist. He is the CEO and co-founder of Hermitage Capital Management, the investment advisor to the Hermitage Fund, which at a time was the largest foreign portfolio investor in Russia.
subtitle: Life as an enemy of the state

title: Crack up capitalism
description: The world is broken up in more ways than just national borders. Join Quinn Slobodian as he explores our recent past to uncover the forces at work behind the scenes and proposes a new theory of capitalism that seeks to free itself from democracy.
speaker_desc: Quinn Slobodian is an author and historian, specialising in modern Germany and international history. He is currently professor of international history at Boston University. He is also contributing writer to New Statesman, co-editor of Contemporary European History and co-director of the History and Political Economy Project. His most recent book is Crack-up Capitalism: Market Radicals and the Dream of a World Without Democracy.
subtitle: Can we free ourselves from democracy?

title: Danger, safety and the future
description: Will future generations still take risks? Join Carol Gilligan, Paul Dolan, and Frank Furedi as they ask if we are being overprotective of future generations in this engaging video debate.
filename: HTLGI2023_L116 Danger, safety and the future.HD.downsized.mp4
speaker_desc: Frank Furedi is an emeritus professor of sociology at the University of Kent, Carol Gilligan is a pioneering feminist and ethicist best known for her revolutionary "ethics of care" theory and Paul Dolan is a leading behavioural scientist and bestselling author, with works like "Happy Ever After" influencing public policy. They join host Isabel Hilton for a debate on our changing relationship with risk.
subtitle: Is risk aversion damaging the next generation?

title: The art of everyday anarchism
description: Is anarchism the absolute freedom of the individual or a chaotic dystopia? Anarchy is one of the most violently divisive political ideals going. Join outspoken theorist, Sophie Scott-Brown, as she sets out her vision of anarchy for everyone.
speaker_desc: Sophie Scott-Brown is the former Director of Gresham College and fellow at the University of St Andrews. An inspiring intellectual historian with research interests in modern European political thought, Anarchism, and the history of education, Sophie is also a fellow of the Higher Education Academy and of the Royal History Society. She is an author excited by historical biography as a means of understanding ideas. Her work includes The Histories of Raphael Samuel: A Portrait of a People’s Historian and Colin Ward and the Art of Everyday Anarchy.
subtitle: Inside anarchy

title: The challenge to optimism
description: Join Nobel Laureate Angus Deaton and the FT's Gillian Tett as they explore the way many people have been left behind by the modern economy and how economics needs to take from philosophy
speaker_desc: Sir Angus Deaton is the Senior Scholar and Professor of Economics at the Princeton School of Public Affair and a Nobel prize-winner. Gillian Tett is an award-winning author, journalist, Provost of King's College Cambridge, and U.S. editor at large at the Financial Times.
subtitle: Economics needs philosophy

title: Physics, particles, and fairytales
description: Many physicists argue that the standard model of particle physics represents our best understanding of the universe. However, it remains unclear how much further it can advance our knowledge.
filename: HTLGI2023_L53 Particles, physics and fairy tales.HD.downsized.mp4
speaker_desc: Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist, author, musician, and science communicator who researches quantum gravity. Gavin Salam is an Oxford-based theoretical physicist celebrated for his groundbreaking work in quantum chromodynamics, the theory describing the strong nuclear force. He was formerly a Senior Research Scientist at CERN and the European Organization for Nuclear Research. Bjørn Ekeberg is a philosopher of science whose main interests lie in the limits of scientific knowledge. He argues that our current understanding of the universe, the Big Bang, and nearly all of Big Bang cosmology is based on faith rather than experimental evidence.
subtitle: Towards the end of the standard model

title: The dream of democracy
description: "Government by the people and for the people" proclaimed Abraham Lincoln. Many argue this principle is under threat. Donors, corporations, the media, and lobbyists are all seen to have more influence. Do we need to outlaw donations and lobbyists, and curtail the influence of corporations and the media? Or is direct government by the people not only impossible to implement but dangerous requiring complex decisions from an electorate that has little expertise?
filename: HTLGI2023 L88 The dream of democracy.crumplepop.downsized.mp4
speaker_desc: Mary Ann Seighart hosts an excellent panel on the future of democracy. Joining her are Nadhim Zahawi, former Chairman of the Conservative Party, Susan Neiman, a daring American philosopher and director of the Einstein Forum in Potsdam, and Philip Collins, Writer-in-Chief at The Draft and former speech writer for Tony Blair.
subtitle: Does money poison politics?

title: Electricity creates consciousness
description: How could calcium ions rushing through a membrane generate the taste of coffee, the smell of a rose or the feeling of love? Join celebrated biochemist, Nick Lane, as he argues that the deep logic of life is at root an electrical phenomenon.
speaker_desc: Nick Lane is an multi-award-winning biochemist and an outstanding science communicator in the origins of life field. He is a Professor of Evolutionary Biochemistry at University College London and a bestselling author of five critically-acclaimed books on evolutionary biochemistry, selling over 150,000 copies worldwide. Transformer: The Deep Chemistry of Life and Death (2022) explores the elusive chemical logic of life, from genetic information to consciousness.
subtitle: Why our idea of consciousness may be wrong

title: How to use adventure for wellbeing
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2023_H238 How to use adventure for wellbeing.HD.mp4
description: Join explorer, entrepreneur and author of best-selling book Adventure Revolution, Belinda Kirk, to discover how adventure can improve our well-being.
filename: HTLGI2023_H238 How to use adventure for wellbeing.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Belinda Kirk is an explorer, entrepreneur and author of best-selling book Adventure Revolution. She is a veteran of fifteen major expeditions and over forty remote filming trips. In 2010, Kirk skippered the first all-female boat to row around Britain.
subtitle: Why it's crucial to leave your comfort zone

title: The AI enigma
description: AI and ChatGPT have changed the world. But is it all hype? Is human intelligence about to be replaced or is this just an apocalyptic fantasy?
speaker_desc: Cognitive scientist Joscha Bach, and AI sceptic and philosopher Mazviita Chirimuuta grapple with the future of intelligence. Hosted by author Cory Doctorow.
subtitle: Is artificial intelligence a threat?

title: The matrix, myths, and metaphysics
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2023 H19 The matrix, myths and metaphysics.downsized.mp4
description: Is there a place for metaphysics in today's society? Join Eric Weinstein, Becky Parker, and Hilary Lawson in this exciting debate on the nature of understanding in times of chaos. Hosted by Joanna Kavenna.
filename: HTLGI2023 H19 The matrix, myths and metaphysics.downsized.mp4
speaker_desc: Eric Weinstein is the host of the premiere podcast The Portal. A doctor of mathematical physics, Eric has proposed that the scientific consensus in physics is broken and radical change in the community is needed. Becky Parker is a renowned physicist who won the first RAS Patrick Moore Medal for outstanding work as a teacher of astronomy. She has received an Honorary Fellowship at the Institute of Physics. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism. He is best known for his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist metaphysics. He is the founder and editorial director of the IAI.
subtitle: Is metaphysics still relevant?

title: Biology beyond genes
description: We tend to think that genes make us who we are. But what if this is the wrong way around? Rather than bottom-up, might nature work top-down? Join biologist, Denis Noble, to explore how organisms create their own destiny using genes.
speaker_desc: One of the pioneers of systems biology, Denis Noble is a Professor Emeritus at the University of Oxford. Renowned for challenging convention, Noble explores the interplay between an organism and its genes.
subtitle: Rethinking evolution

title: Frank Furedi | Interview
description: Frank Furedi is a political philosopher at the heart of the culture war. Join him in this thought-provoking interview on the state of identity in modern society.
speaker_desc: Frank Furedi is a emeritus professor of sociology at the University of Kent. Since the late 1990s, he has been widely cited about his views on why Western societies find it so difficult to engage with risk and uncertainty. His book Invitation to Terror: expanding the empire of the unknown explores the way in which the threat of terrorism has become amplified through the ascendancy of precautionary thinking.
subtitle: On rethinking identity

title: Naming and shaming
description: Critics argue contemporary mechanisms of shame, like cyberbullying, 'fat shaming', and cancel culture, have spiralled dangerously out of control. Join Joanna Kavenna, Sophie Scott-Brown, and Peter Tatchell as they debate the efficacy of shame in society in this thought-provoking video.
speaker_desc: Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning novelist. Sophie Scott-Brown is a prestigious intellectual historian, a lecturer at the University of Oxford, and a Director of the Europaeum Institute of European History. Peter Tatchell is an inspiring human rights campaigner, a member of the gay rights group Outrage!, and director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation, a human rights organization. Florence Read hosts.
subtitle: Do we need shame for social progress?

title: The centre of the universe
description: We see Copernicus as a providing a key moment in history where we moved on from seeing ourselves at the centre of the universe. Join Neil Turok, Lisa Randall, and Martin Cohen as they debate the role of anthropocentrism in physics in this exciting video.
filename: HTLGI2023_H141 The centre of the universe.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Lisa Randall is an Honorary Fellow of the Institute of Physics and Frank B. Baird, Jr. Professor of Science on the physics faculty of Harvard University. She has been named one of the most promising theoretical physicists of her generation. Neil Turok is a preeminent mathematical physicist. He is the inaugural Higgs Chair of Theoretical Physics at the University of Edinburgh and director emeritus of the Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics. Martin Cohen is a multitalented philosopher, author and journalist who has become a household name in popular philosophy. His books include the bestseller ‘101 Philosophy Problems’, now published in a dozen languages.
subtitle: Does science carry a human bias?

title: Jimena Canales Interview
description: Join award-winning science historian Jimena Canales in this studio interview as she discusses the process of discovery and the nature of the unknown in science.
speaker_desc: Jimena Canales is a pioneering historian of science and an expert in 19th and 20th century history of the physical sciences. She is currently Vice-President of the Board of the American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS).
subtitle: On scientists and their demons

title: Mental health reimagined
description: We often view depression as a disorder. But could this be a mistake? Join front-line psychiatrist, Mark Salter, as he argues that depression is not an illness, rather a process, in this insightful talk.
speaker_desc: Mark Salter is a consultant psychiatrist based in London’s East End, specialising in risk, untowardness and media portrayals of mental distress.
subtitle: Why we should value the awful

title: The Life and Philosophy of Alastair Campbell
description: Since retiring from front-line politics, Alastair Campbell has become editor-at-large at The New European, hosts "The Rest is Politics" podcast with Rory Stewart, and authored the acclaimed book, 'But What Can I Do?' Explore his extraordinary life and philosophy in this filmed conversation hosted by Philip Collins.
speaker_desc: Formerly Director of Communications for Tony Blair's New Labour government, Alastair Campbell is now an editor-at-large at The New European, has launched with Rory Stewart the most successful political podcast in the UK, 'The Rest Is Politics', and authored the acclaimed book, 'But What Can I Do?'
subtitle: Brexit, Labour and the problem with politics

title: Fragments and reality
description: Join Michael Della Rocca, Tim Maudlin, Kathleen Higgins as they discuss the fundamental nature of reality in this engaging video debate. Hosted by Jack Symes.
speaker_desc: Jack Symes is the producer of The Panpsycast Philosophy Podcast and editor of the Bloomsbury series Talking about Philosophy. He is currently Teacher and Researcher at Durham University, UK. Michael Della Rocca is Sterling Professor of Philosophy at Yale University and author of The Parmenidean Ascent. Tim Maudlin is Professor of Philosophy at New York University and the Founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics. Kathleen Higgins is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin and the author of Comic Relief: Nietzsche's “Gay Science”.
subtitle: Is the world really made of separate parts?

title: Fascist passions
description: Judith Butler, pioneering gender theorist whose changed the way we think about gender and sexuality, explores the topic of their most recent book, in this compelling talk where they offer a powerful diagnosis of the fears that make up today's wars on gender.
speaker_desc: Judith Butler is Distinguished Professor in the Graduate School and formerly the Maxine Elliot Chair in the Department of Comparative Literature and the Program of Critical Theory at the University of California, Berkeley. They are most well-known for their ground-breaking book Gender Trouble (1990) and their theory of performativity.
subtitle: Judith Butler on the animosity toward gender

title: In conversation: Sabine Hossenfelder and Hilary Lawson
description: Join physicist Sabine Hossenfelder and non-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson in riveting conversation. With Hilary interviewing, Sabine outlines her attitude to the problems of modern physics and the importance of philosophy.
speaker_desc: Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist, author, musician, and science communicator who researches quantum gravity. Hilary is a non-realist philosopher known for his theory of closure.
subtitle: On physics' need for philosophy

title: Democratic capitalism in crisis
description: Capitalism as we know it is in crisis. Slow growth, inflation and widening inequality makes for a worrying potion. But how do we fix this? Join chief economics commentator of the FT, Martin Wolf, as he offers his cure for this crisis. Hosted by Sergei Guriev, Provost of Science Po.
speaker_desc: Martin Wolf is Associate Editor and Chief Economics Commentator at the Financial Times, London. He was awarded the CBE (Commander of the British Empire) in 2000 for services to financial journalism. Sergei Guriev is a Russian economist, who is provost and a professor of economics at the Institut d'études politiques in Paris. From 2016 to 2019, he was the chief economist at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
subtitle: Has the snake eaten its own tail?

title: Consciousness and material reality
description: Join physicist and philosopher, Avshalom C. Elitzur as he makes a radical new proposal about the relationship between consciousness and material reality in this thought-provoking talk.
speaker_desc: Avshalom C. Elitzur is a Professor in the Centre for Quantum Studies at Chapman University in the United States. He is best known for his work on the Elitzur–Vaidman bomb-testing problem in quantum mechanics.
subtitle: Thinking outside the laws of physics

title: Creativity and freedom
description: In a world where creativity is cherished, freedom of expression is under scrutiny. Instances like Salman Rushdie's stabbing and Jay Z's battle against lyrics used in court raise concerns. The prospect of censoring authors like Roald Dahl and their works is alarming. With the rise of sensitivity readers, should writers and artists be shielded from retribution, even if their views offend? Or should certain expressions be banned to fight prejudice? Is it time to reaffirm Western liberal values or challenge the authority of liberalism?
speaker_desc: Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning novelist, essayist, and travel writer. Her latest book, Zed, is a brilliant tale of big-tech dystopia and life under a global media tech corporation. Jolyon Maugham is an activist barrister. As founder of the Good Law Project, Jolyon has challenged the UK government's approach to Brexit, Covid, and transgender rights.
