title: A better tomorrow
description: The majority of Westerners believe the world is getting worse when asked. Yet in key metrics such as extreme poverty and life expectancy, things are improving globally. Is our pessimism an error? Or is progress driven by dissatisfaction with the status quo?
speaker_desc: Isabel Hilton is the founder and and editor of chinadialogue.net, and is a former editor-in-chief of opendemocracy.net. As CEO, she oversees China Dialogue's efforts to stoke discussion about the environment between Chinese and non-Chinese sources Shaun Bailey AM is a distinguished politician and former journalist who famously led the 2021 Conservative campaign in London as the party's candidate for Mayor of London. Thangam Debbonaire is the Labour MP for Bristol West and current Shadow Leader of the House of Commons, previously working as the Shadow Secretary of State for Housing. Michael Bocirkiw is an acclaimed writer, global affairs analyst whose been on the frontline teams at many international humanitarian organizations. He is the esteemed author of Digital Pandemic- Covid-19: How Tech Went From Bad to Good.
subtitle: Is the world getting better or worse?

title: Getting everything, losing everything
description: Virtual reality was once the stuff of science fiction, but is now a widely available technology. Its proponents suggest living more in the digital world will allow more people to access experiences currently only available to a few. Is a digital society an inevitable part of our future? Or this a dystopian nightmare that threatens human connection and vitality?
speaker_desc: Maria Balaska is currently a research fellow at the University of Hertfordshire and at Åbo Akademi University. Anders Sandberg is a researcher, popular science debater, trans-humanist and author of Superhuman: Exploring Human Enhancement from 600 BCE to 2050. Massimo Pigliucci is a philosophy professor at the City College of New York and former co-host of the Rationally Speaking Podcast. His research interests include the Philosophy of Science and the Philosophy of Biology. Mazviita Chirimuuta is a Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Edinburgh. She is a self-described techno-pessimist and anti-transhumanist.
subtitle: The dawn of a new reality?

title: The demons of thermodynamics
description: Thermodynamics and the problem of entropy has puzzled scientists for many years. Join philosopher of physics Katie Robertson as she explores how we might exorcise the demons of thermodynamics.
speaker_desc: Katie Robertson is a research fellow and cutting edge philosopher of physics at the University of Birmingham. Her research focuses on the role that entropy plays in black holes.
subtitle: Seeing the world through the geometry of chaos

title: Democracy is dead
description: In the wake of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the West has signalled a renewed commitment to democracy and freedom. But will this be enough to halt the rise of global authoritarianism?
speaker_desc: Calvin Robinson is a political commentator, journalist, policy advisor and campaigner who is a senior fellow at the research institute Policy Exchange. Robinson worked as a secondary school teacher and became a video games journalist. He is a regular contributor to The Daily Telegraph and the Daily Mail.
subtitle: Does the future hold a new authoritarianism?

title: The seduction of thought
description: Ever since the Enlightenment, Western culture has valued reason and thought highly. We spent most of our time puzzling, planning or pondering. But is this is a mistake? Might culture be better off were it to, in Nietzsche's words, 'free itself from the seduction of words and thought'?
speaker_desc: Bestselling author Miranda Keeling, psychologist Steve Taylor and prison philosopher Andy West decide: to think, or not to think? Janne Teller hosts.
subtitle: Is thought a distraction from reality?

title: The strangeness of the universe
description: Niels Bohr suggested the universe is stranger than we could possibly imagine. Was he right? Will science and philosophy ever be able to accurately capture the fundamental laws of the universe? Or should we accept that the mysteries of the universe will always transcend human understanding?
filename: HTLGI2022_H182 The strangeness of the universe.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Influential scientist Rupert Sheldrake, prominent physicist Sabine Hossenfelder and esteemed philosopher Bjørn Ekeberg get to grips with whether the universe is stranger than we can imagine. Johnjoe McFadden hosts.
subtitle: A weird and wonderful world

title: Logic for the left
description: In an age where the left are regularly accused of priotising feelings over facts, can the left reclaim logic? Join philosopher and Marxist Ben Burgis as he debunks contemporary political myths.
speaker_desc: Ben Burgis is a philosophy professor at Morehouse University Perimeter College, a columnist for Jacobin Magazine and Arc Digital Media, and the co-host of the Dead Pundits Society. He also used to have a regular segment on The Michael Brooks Show called "the Debunk." Burgis is the author of several books including' Give Them an Argument: Logic for the Left' and 'Christopher Hitchens: What He Got Right, How He Went Wrong, and Why He Still Matters'.
subtitle: Why rationality is important for the left

title: The evolution of war
description: Is the urge to go to war part of humanity's evolutionary make-up? Join trailblazing researcher Bonaventura Majolo as he explores whether the propensity for war is in our DNA.
speaker_desc: Known for his trailbrazing research on cooperation, aggression, altruism, and war, Bonaventura Majolo is Professor of Social Evolution at the University of Lincoln.
subtitle: Are we made to go to war?

title: Forbidden Fruit
description: We've never talked so openly about sex. But is this frankness devaluing the very things that make sex appealing? Are romance, intimacy and mystery undermined in a society that is so casual about sex?
speaker_desc: Journalist Zoe Strimpel, radical social theorist Myriam François and writer Louise Perry fight over forbidden fruit. Hosted by Rana Mitter.
subtitle: Sex and taboo in the modern age

title: Fact-checking the fact-checkers
description: In a world where truth is always in doubt, how should we approach organisations that present themselves as fact-checkers? Should we recognise that nations and individuals always embed a biased perspective? Or is it possible to promote a public discourse rooted in fact?
speaker_desc: Renowned journalist Paul Mason, author of Technology is Not Neutral Stephanie Hare and UnHerd editor Freddie Sayers debate the facts behind the facts. Hilary Lawson hosts.
subtitle: Is it possible for fact checking to be impartial?

title: How philosophy got lost
description: Globally renowned philosopher Slavoj Žižek takes us on a whirlwind tour of continental philosophy, Hegel's insights into contemporary political crises, the Covid-19 pandemic and how philosophy is like falling in love.
speaker_desc: Slavoj Žižek is a globally renowned philosopher and cultural critic. He is international director of the Birkbeck Institute for the Humanities at the University of London, visiting professor at New York University and a senior researcher at the University of Ljubljana's Department of Philosophy. He is the author of several books, including The Sublime Object of Ideology, The Parallax View, Living in the End Times and Heaven in Disorder.
subtitle: An interview with philosopher Slavoj Žižek

title: Material girls
description: The conversation surrounding transgender rights is often divisive and unproductive. Join philosopher Kathleen Stock as she sets out her position on gender and biology, and how trans activists and feminist can unite for a less polarised future.
speaker_desc: Kathleen Mary Linn Stock OBE is a British philosopher and writer. She was a professor of philosophy at the University of Sussex until 2021. She has published academic work on aesthetics, fiction, imagination, sexual objectification, and sexual orientation.
subtitle: Kathleen Stock’s perspective on sex and gender

title: Beyond the Darkness
description: Dark matter has been put forward by scientists as a way to understand previously unexplainable aspects of our cosmos. But after much searching, scientists have not been able to discover dark matter particles. Is it time to radically reassess the dark matter paradigm? Or is a breakthrough discovery just around the corner?
speaker_desc: Trailblazing philosopher Bjørn Ekeberg, theoretical physicist Francesca Chadha-Day and influential astrophysicist Pavel Kroupa explore the many mysteries of dark matter. John-Joe McFadden hosts.
subtitle: Dark Matter: A Baseless Hypothesis?

title: Truth, delusion and psychedelic reality
description: Psychedelics are being put forward as a potentially radical treatment for mental illness. But is this short-sighted? Will psychedelics replace mental illness with a distorted view of reality? Or can they help those suffering break out of unhelpful psychological paradigms?
filename: HTLGI2022_L45 Truth, delusion and psychedelic reality.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: KCL psychiatrist James Rucker, philosopher Julian Baggini, and creative director and artist Eileen Hall debate psychedelics and science. Hosted by leading psychiatrist Mark Salter.
subtitle: Are psychedelics a window into reality?

title: There is no Planet B
description: Acclaimed writer and researcher Mike Berners-Lee tackles the most common misconceptions surrounding climate change and argues for how we might achieve structural change.
speaker_desc: Mike Berners-Lee is a pre-eminent expert in carbon footprinting and Professor and Fellow of the Institute for Social Futures at Lancaster University. He is also the director and principal consultant at Small World Consulting and the author of three books, including There Is No Planet B: A Handbook for the Make or Break Years.
subtitle: An interview with Mike Berners-Lee

title: The science of uncertainty with Tim Palmer
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2022_H208 The Science of Uncertainty Tim Palmer.HD.ve.mp4
description: We have all grown accustomed to living with uncertainty in recent years. But what are the scientific and mathematic forces governing uncertainty? Join acclaimed professor Tim Palmer as he argues that understanding uncertainty is crucial to progress.
filename: HTLGI2022_H208 The Science of Uncertainty Tim Palmer.HD.ve.mp4
subtitle: Uncertainty as the essence of understanding

title: Society 2.0
description: The pandemic opened our eyes to the jobs society can't live without. In the wake of Covid-19, should we prioritise key workers and abandon the idea that professional and managerial jobs are the best paid? Or should we still reward university education and a white-collar career with the highest wages?
speaker_desc: Member of the Shadow Cabinet House Thangam Debbonaire, Radio 6 DJ and psychotherapist Nemone Metaxas and Marxist philosopher Ben Burgis explore the undervalued people in our society. Hosted by Mary-Ann Sieghart.
subtitle: Do we unfairly privilege the unelected?

title: Being ourselves and being with others
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2022_L115 Being ourselves and being with others.HD.mp4
description: In recent decades we have emphasised the importance of individualism, self-expression and self-sufficiency. Yet studies suggest we aren't happier for it. Is it time to let go of our attachment to independence and embrace a more communal way of living? Or is this a naive view which ignores how unique we all are?
filename: HTLGI2022_L115 Being ourselves and being with others.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Critically-acclaimed writer Janne Teller, world leading psychologist and psychiatrist Stefan Priebe, and actress-writer and Booker Prize nominee Sophie Ward debate the lures of loneliness. Hosted by renowned journalist Elaine Glaser.
subtitle: Has independence undermined community?

title: Why Dawkins is wrong
description: The sequencing of genetic information was expected to usher in a breakthrough in medical cures for illnesses, yet this hasn't happened. Join esteemed biologist Denis Noble as he argues our approach to biology is the wrong way round.
speaker_desc: Oxford Professor and one of the pioneers of Systems Biology, Noble developed the first viable mathematical model of the working heart in 1960.
subtitle: An interview with the renowned biologist

title: In conversation with Peter Tatchell and Bobbi Pickard
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2022_H255 Talking together with Peter Tatchell and Bobbi Pickard.HD.mp4
description: Legendary activist Peter Tatchell and trans rights campaigner Bobbi Pickard unpick the fiery debate over transgender rights, and offer a path for society to move forward.
filename: HTLGI2022_H255 Talking together with Peter Tatchell and Bobbi Pickard.HD.mp4
subtitle: A response to trans critics

title: The ignorance of experts
description: Science is the belief in the ignorance of experts, argued Richard Feynman. Was he right to suggest that science is not a learnt set of facts, but a constantly evolving method of discovering knowledge? Or, in a world under threat from health crises such as Covid-19, do we need to treat science as an authority in order to get the best outcomes?
speaker_desc: Author of How The World Thinks Julian Baggini, philosopher of biology Ellen Clarke, and radical philosopher Ben Burgis tackle our diminishing trust in experts and what to do about it. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
subtitle: Can we rely on science for the answers?

title: The accurate, the perfect and the dangerous
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2022_L106 The accurate, the perfect and the dangerous.HD.mp4
description: We tend to think of data and technology as impartial tools that can deliver us results free from human prejudice. But from sexist chatbots to racist algorithms, it seems our data is always coloured by human fallibility. Do we need to give up on the idea that data is impartial? Or is our technology not yet sophisticated enough to transcend our human flaws?
filename: HTLGI2022_L106 The accurate, the perfect and the dangerous.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Futurist Anders Sandberg, Oxford bioethicist Michael Parker and author of Technology is Not Neutral Stephanie Hare fight for the future of tech, data and AI. Hosted by pioneering economist Linda Yueh.
subtitle: The potential and the threat of data

title: Are we facing a new world order?
description: Nigel Inkster discusses China's rise as a cyberpower, and who is seizing the upperhand on the world stage
speaker_desc: Nigel Inkster is the distinguished former director of intelligence for the British Intelligence Service, and now Director of Intelligence Analysis at Enodo Economics.
subtitle: Interview with Nigel Inkster

title: How to see the world through Kafka's eyes
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2022_H194 How to see the world through Kafka's eyes.HD.mp4
description: Over a century since it was published, how can Kafka's Metamorphosis help us gain insights into the pressures of modernity? Join acclaimed actor and director Steven Berkoff as he helps see the world through Kafka's eyes.
filename: HTLGI2022_H194 How to see the world through Kafka's eyes.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Steven Berkoff is an actor, author, playwright, theatre practitioner and theatre director. He is noted for his roles in the James Bond film, ‘Octopussy’, A Clockwork Orange, and The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo. On the stage, he has performed the title roles in Shakespeare’s Hamlet, Richard II and Macbeth. He is recognised for his brand of “Berkovian theatre", which combines elements of physical theatre, total theatre and expressionism.
subtitle: Unmasking the human condition

title: The equality myth
description: Despite advances in women's rights over the last 50 years, many surveys show women's happiness has decreased in this time. Is it time to refocus feminism towards goals of personal fulfilment rather than political equality with men? Or is this reported dissatisfaction itself a sign that women are now empowered to speak out about their lives?
speaker_desc: Journalist and writer Laurie Penny, Shadow Leader of the Commons, Thangam Debbonaire and campaigner-author Louise Perry try to tip the scales. Hosted by Oxford historian Rana Mitter.
subtitle: Is the pursuit of absolute equality a mistake?

title: The democracy illusion
description: Do politicans matter? Many people across the world feel that change rarely materialises in their ordinary lives, no matter who they vote for. Are politicians the public face for an unnaccountable network of technical decision-makers? Or is this apathetic mindset precisely what the ruling class depend on to sustain their rule?
speaker_desc: Trailblazing journalist Calvin Robinson, social activist Shabnam Nasimi, and radical journalist Aaron Bastani debate the changing face of democracy in the 21st century. Hosted by Manveen Rana.
subtitle: Do elected politicians make a difference?

title: Head to Head: Philosophy vs Science
description: Historically, philosophy and science have been united as complementary methods of investigating life's fundamental questions. But since the Enlightenment the two have drifted apart and even become antagonistic. Join prize-winning physicist Marika Taylor and philosopher Julian Baggini as they discuss the relationship between the two fields.
speaker_desc: Marika Taylor is a Professor of Theoretical Physics and the Head of School within Mathematical Sciences at University of Southampton. Taylor's research is focussed on string theory, quantum field theory and gravitational physics. Julian Baggini is a philosopher, journalist, author and the co-founder of The Philosopher's Magazine. He is the acclaimed author of over 20 works of popular philosophy. Güneş Taylor hosts.
subtitle: Does science need philosophy?

title: Deconstructing the art of storytelling
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2022_H281 How to keep your audience hooked.HD.mp4
description: How do you create great stories that keep your audience hooked? Join three-time Olivier Award-nominated playwright Danny Robbins as he reveals the secrets of effective storytelling
filename: HTLGI2022_H281 How to keep your audience hooked.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Danny Robins is an award-winning British writer, broadcaster and journalist. His most recent play, 2:22 A Ghost Story, has received much critical acclaim.
subtitle: How to keep your audience hooked

title: The theory to end all theories
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2022_L97 The theory to end all theories.HD.NEW.mp4
description: Physics' theory of everything was supposed to be just around the corner. Now it looks less likely than ever. Can any scientific theory ever be more than a model?
filename: HTLGI2022_L97 The theory to end all theories.HD.NEW.mp4
speaker_desc: Theoretical physicist Peter Woit, physicist and educator Becky Parker and critic of realism Hilary Lawson test their theories of everything. Hosted by award-winning science documentary filmmaker David Malone.
subtitle: Is a theory of everything possible?

title: The key to consciousness
description: Modern neuroscience has brought us no closer to solving the mystery of consciousness. Can this puzzle ever be detached from the dichotomy of subject and object?
speaker_desc: Revolutionary cognitive psychologist Donald Hoffman (joining us live from across the pond), neuroscientist Hannah Critchlow and philosopher Sam Coleman battle to unlock consciousness. Hosted by award-winning novelist Joanna Kavenna.
subtitle: Is materialism a fundamental mistake?

title: Rebellion and rebirth
description: What does it take for a person to heal from sexual trauma, and for society to adequately deal with the issue? Join activist and performance artist Emma Sulkowicz as she discusses her personal journey of rebellion and rebirth.
speaker_desc: Emma Sulkowicz is a performance artist living and working in New York City, most famous for her year-long performance art project Mattress Performance: Carry That Weight where she dragged a mattress around Columbia University in protest at the school’s mishandling of her sexual assault complaint, and becoming one of the faces of the movement against rape culture on college campuses.
subtitle: What activism teaches us about the world

title: The future of cosmology with Roger Penrose
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2022_H166 The Future of Cosmology with Roger Penrose HD v2.mp4
description: Join Nobel Prize-winning mathematician Roger Penrose and philosopher of science Katie Robertson as they discuss the forces that govern our cosmos and the equations which define our reality.
filename: HTLGI2022_H166 The Future of Cosmology with Roger Penrose HD v2.mp4
subtitle: Is the universe reborn in cycles?

title: After happily ever after
description: We expect closure from our stories. Does this reflect a desire for our fictional worlds to have order when our real one doesn't? Or are non-narrative structures doomed to be alienating and unsuccessful?
speaker_desc: Academy award nominee David Hare, critically acclaimed writer Janne Teller and director-producer Sophie Fiennes talk endings. Hosted by Barry Smith, Director of the Institute of Philosophy.
subtitle: Do our lives tell a story?

title: Gravitational waves: a new frontier?
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2022_H87 Gravity a new window on the universe v1 HD.mp4
description: Join world-renowned physicist Paul Davies as he uncovers the importance of gravitational waves and why they might be the answer to some of the most complex problems in physics
filename: HTLGI2022_H87 Gravity a new window on the universe v1 HD.mp4
subtitle: Black holes, gravity and the future of cosmology

title: Feminism and identity politics
description: Celebrated journalist and author Yasmin Alibhai-Brow explores whether identity politics and feminism are compatible.
speaker_desc: Award-winning, Ugandan-born author and columnist Yasmin Alibhai-Brown currently writes for The Independent and The Evening Standard, and is the founder of British Muslims for Secular Democracy.
subtitle: Is identity politics holding feminism back?

title: The future of freedom
description: A famed experiment by Libet in the 1980s claimed to demonstrate that free will was an illusion. Despite frequent challenges, the legacy of this idea looms over philosophy. Are we really just pre-programmed biological machines or can we shape our own destinies?
speaker_desc: Prolific British writer, philosopher and co-founder of The Philosophers’ Magazine, Julian Baggini, renowned Australian philosopher of science, Peter Godfrey-Smith, and leading British neuroscientist and UCL professor, Sarah Garfinkel, argue about empiricism and its role in determining the existence of free will. Alex O'Connor hosts.
subtitle: Can experiments settle the free will debate?

title: Science fact or science fiction?
description: Since the Enlightenment, we have made sure our scientific theories can be tested and produce empirical evidence. But many of today's most popular scientific theories - from the multiverse to string theory - have no way of being empirically tested. Should we conclude that these theories are pure speculation and unscientific? Or is it enough for a theory to be internally coherent?
speaker_desc: Harry Cliff is a particle physicist at the University of Cambridge working on the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. A prominent promoter for the public's understanding of physics, Harry is also the author of the popular science book, How To Make An Apple Pie From Scratch. Tim Maudlin is a world leading researcher in the foundations of physics, metaphysics, and logic. He is a Professor of Philosophy at NYU and Founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics. Marika Taylor is one of the foremost researchers of string theory, quantum field theory and gravitational physics. Having completed her doctoral dissertation under Stephen Hawking, Taylor went onto be Professor of Theoretical Physics and head of Mathematical Physics at the University of Southampton. Barry C Smith is a professor of philosophy and directs the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study. He is the founding director of the Centre for the Study of Sensess.
subtitle: Are some scientific theories fictional speculation

title: The enduring trauma of the caste system
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2020_G92 The reality behind the caste system.HD.mp4
description: What role does the caste system play in Hindu society? Join Indian economist Ashwini Deshpande as she uncovers the reality of a social system cloaked in mystery for most Westerners.
filename: HTLGI2020_G92 The reality behind the caste system.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Ashwini Deshpande is an Indian economist best known for her papers concerning various topics such as poverty, inequality, regional disparities and gender discrimination. She is currently working as a professor at Ashoka University, and formerly taught at Delhi School of Economics.
subtitle: Overcoming prejudice and brutal discrimination

title: A tale of truth with Simon Blackburn
description: Is there anything as contested as 'the truth'? Join renowned philosopher Simon Blackburn as he explores the difficulty of discerning truth in the modern age, and why pragmatism may be the best approach.
speaker_desc: Author of Think and Truth: A Guide for the Perplexed , Simon Blackburn has worked to bring philosophy to a wider audience. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Cambridge University and Vice President of the British Humanist Association.
subtitle: The case against relativism

title: The happiness delusion
description: Should society's main goal be the happiness of its citizens? Should governments put happiness at the centre of their policy-making? Or is obsessing over happiness a counterproductive mistake?
speaker_desc: Aaron Bastani is co-founder of Novara Media, an independent, self-described radical left-wing alternative media organisation. He is also the author ‘Fully Automated Luxury Communism’. Paul Dolan is a behavioural scientist and author of the bestselling book ‘Happiness By Design: Finding Pleasure and Purpose in Everyday Life.’ Joanna Kavenna is a multi-award-winning writer. She was named as one of Granta’s Best Young British Novelists for her ground-breaking novels including A Field Guide to Reality and Zed. Regular presenter of Night Waves and writer for the Financial Times, History Today, and the London Review of Books, Rana Mitter is Professor of the History and Politics of Modern China at Oxford.
subtitle: In search of the aim of life

title: The weaker sex?
description: In a post-feminist age, it is normal for women to be considered equal to men is most fields. Yet during war it is still standard for men to fight and for women to stay at home. Is this an understandable reflection of biological differences? Or an outdated patriarchal notion that women need 'defending' by men?
speaker_desc: Mary Ann Sieghart is a journalist and radio presenter and a former assistant editor of The Times . Her latest book is The Authority Gap: Why Women Are Still Taken Less Seriously Than Men . Minna Salami is journalist, feminist and author. She has written on the experiences of Nigerian women, the African Diaspora and feminism through her award-winning blog, MsAfropolitan . Her latest book is Sensuous Knowledge . Maya Oppenheim is Women's Correspondent for the Independent and writes on issues of domestic violence, sexual assault, abortion and period poverty. Rana Mitter is a regular presenter of Night Waves and writer for the Financial Times , History Today , and the London Review of Books . He is also a Professor of the History and Politics of Modern China at the University of Oxford.
subtitle: Do women still need 'protecting' from men?

title: The making of reality
description: The grand metaphysical narratives we have inherited assume the world is divided into discrete entities, which can we study and define. But what if this approach is wrong? Join post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson as he takes us through his theory of Closure and argues that we 'close' the openness of the world with our thought and language.
speaker_desc: Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and a renowned critic of philosophical realism. He is best known for his work on reflexivity and his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist metaphysics arguing that we close the openness of the world with our thought and language.
subtitle: An interview with Hilary Lawson

title: The mystery of prehistory
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2022 H 25 The Mystery of Prehistory HD.mp4
description: Take a journey back through time with TV anthropologist Mary-Anna Ochota as she explores the surprising secrets of Britain's prehistoric people
filename: HTLGI2022 H 25 The Mystery of Prehistory HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Known best for her work as a presenter, Mary-Ann Ochota specialises in anthropology, archaeology and social history. She co-presented Channel 4’s cult archaeology show ‘Time Team’, and recently fronted the hugely successful ‘Feral Children’ series.
subtitle: What makes us who we are?

title: The medicine myth
description: Many futurists have believed that death is merely a technical problem science will one day solve. But living in the shadow of the Covid-19 pandemic, do we still believe in the absolute power of medicine to fight disease? Or do we need to accept we cannot be super-human and embrace mortality?
speaker_desc: Denis Noble is a world renowned biologist, and Professor Emeritus of Cardiovascular Physiology at the University of Oxford. Famous for developing the first mathematical model of cardiac cells. Nessa Carey is a ground-breaking British biologist working in the field of molecular biology and biotechnology. She is International Director of the technology transfer organization PraxisUnico and a Visiting Professor at Imperial College London. Guy Brown heads a research group at the University of Cambridge working on cell death in the brain, the heart and in cancer. His previous book The Energy of Life won the Wellcome Trust Prize for popular science. David Malone is an independent filmmaker, Green Party politician, and author of The Debt Generation.
subtitle: The failure of medicalising philosophy

title: The passion of reason
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2022 L_76 The Passion of Reason HD.mp4
description: For centuries we have believed in the separation of reason and emotion. But are we mistaken in ignoring how connected the two are? Is it time to rethink the way we think?
filename: HTLGI2022 L_76 The Passion of Reason HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Philosopher and acclaimed author, Julian Baggini, leading molecular biologist, Güneş Taylor, and critical race theorist, Tommy Curry, put passion and reason to the test.
subtitle: Does emotion rule over reason?

title: Fiction, social construction and gender
description: What's the difference between sex and gender? Should individuals' private expressions of non-conforming gender be protected by law? Outspoken gender critical feminist Kathleen Stock outlines her unique views on gender, sex, philosophy and fiction
speaker_desc: Kathleen Mary Linn Stock OBE is a British philosopher and writer. She was a professor of philosophy at the University of Sussex until 2021. She has published academic work on aesthetics, fiction, imagination, sexual objectification, and sexual orientation.
subtitle: Freedom, truth and trans rights

title: How Occam's Razor changed the world
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2021_82 How Occam's Razor changed the world.HD.mp4
description: Modern science and the scientific method owe a lot to a 14th-century monk named Occam. Join quantum biologist Johnjoe McFadden as he explores how Occam's Razor, with its preference for simplicity, cut through superstition and medieval religion to help us understand the world more clearly.
filename: HTLGI2021_82 How Occam's Razor changed the world.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Johnjoe McFadden is a Professor of Modular Genetics at the University of Surrey and the author of Quantum Revolution. His work focuses on how quantum mechanics influences our biology and the use of quantum theory to uncover alternative evolutionary frameworks.
subtitle: The value of simplicity in a complex world

title: Is it moral to trade with the devil?
description: Free trade has historically been seen as a force for good, both financially and diplomatically. But has Europe's dependence on Russian oil, and the unstoppable growth of China, shown this to be a fundamental mistake?
speaker_desc: Andrew Adonis is a Labour Politian, leading journalist and academic. John Kay is a bestselling author and one of the UK's most renowned economists. Janne Teller is a novelist and former conflict advisor for the UNO and EU. Hosting this debate is journalist and columnist at the Irish Times, Finn McRedmond.
subtitle: Trading with the enemy

title: Love and other drugs
description: We tend to view love and romance as organic. But scientific and anecdotal evidence has shown that psychoactive substances can enhance our feelings of love for others. Is time we let go of organic love as an antiquated ideal and embrace drugs as a means of 'hacking' love?
speaker_desc: Anders Sandberg is a research fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute at Oxford, where his research focusses on the societal and ethical issues surrounding human enhancement and new technologies. He is also research associate at the Oxford Uehiro Centre for Practical Ethics and the Oxford Centre for Neuroethics. A regular commentator and participant of public debates concerning human enhancement, Anders comes to the festival in support of an exciting transhuman future. On Twitter he describes himself as an academic jack of all trades, and we are sure he is a master of some. Ella Whelan is a political commentator and freelance journalist. After graduating in 2014, Whelan joined online politics magazine spiked, and quickly rose to assistant editor. She is a producer of the annual Battle of Ideas Festival in central London and writes for the Sunday Times, the Irish Times, the Sun and The Economist. Whelan regularly appears in the media; her support for Brexit and criticism of no-platforming and 21st century feminism has caused her to clash with mainstream journalists on the BBC, Sky, and Channel 4. Her first book, What Women Want: Fun, Freedom and an End to Feminism, was described as "a leading voice of a rising generation of young warriors for free speech" by distinguished social critic Camille Paglia. She wrote Inferior: How Science Got Women Wrong in 2017. Her book Superior: The Return of Race Science addresses the racial biases present in current scientific practices. Rupert Sheldrake is a biologist and bestselling author. Best known for his 2012 book 'The Science Delusion' and the controversial, viral TED talk he gave which was banned by the organisation. He’s a Distinguished Supporter of Humanists UK, Atkins is outspoken in his opposition to religion. subtitle: The Secret Life of Clothes

title: Mary-Jane Rubenstein | In-depth Interview
description: Multiverse research is providing new information about where we come from and the nature of the universe, which could radically impact faith as well as physics.
speaker_desc: Mary-Jane Rubenstein is Professor of Religion, Feminist, Gender and Sexuality Studies at Wesleyan University. She is the author of Strange Wonder: The Closure of Metaphysics and the Opening of Awe, Worlds without End: The Many Lives of the Multiverse, and most recently, Pantheologies: Gods, Worlds, Monsters.
subtitle: On the multiverse, pantheism, and beyond

title: The Universe That Wasn't There
description: Dark Matter and Dark Energy supposedly account for 95% of the universe, but we still can’t detect them. Roger Penrose, Subir Sarkar, and Catherine Heymans consider why.
speaker_desc: World-renowned physicist Roger Penrose, Head of Particle Theory at Oxford Professor Subir Sarkar, and Professor of Astrophysics Catherine Heymans wonder why we can't find most of the universe. David Malone hosts.
subtitle: In search of dark matter and dark energy

title: The True and the Trivial
description: Nietzsche and Derrida argued rony and comedy are central to deep philosophical thought. Justin Smith, Barry C Smith and Joanna Kavena as if ideas need to be serious to have lasting impact, or can humour convey profound insight?
speaker_desc: Philosopher and author of Irrationality Justin Smith, Director of the Institute of Philosophy Barry C. Smith, and author of Inglorious Joanna Kavenna unravel the relationship between humour and serious ideas. Philosopher Robert Rowland Smith hosts .
subtitle: Can comedy convey profound ideas?

title: Tim Maudlin | In-depth Interview
description: Philosopher of science Tim Maudlin discusses interpretations of quantum mechanics, pilot wave theory and objective collapse theory.
speaker_desc: Tim Maudlin, author of Philosophy of Physics, is an American philosopher of science responsible for influential works on metaphysical foundations of physics and logic.
subtitle: On Quantum Theory and where it might take us

title: Massimo Pigliucci | In-depth Interview
description: Philosopher Massimo Pigliucci makes the case for adopting stoicism as a philosophy to live by, and why scepticism is still relevant today.
subtitle: On stoicism, scepticism, and pseudoscience

title: Susan Neiman | In-depth Interview
description: Moral philosopher Susan Neiman examines the nature of Evil and our fascination with it, from evil-doers in pop culture to what Hannah Arendt called banal evils.
speaker_desc: Susan Neiman, author of Evil in Modern Thought and Moral Clarity: A Guide for Grown-Up Idealists , is a moral philosopher and director of the Einstein Forum in Potsdam.
subtitle: On Evil and it's allure

title: Donald Hoffman | In-depth Interview
description: Donald Hoffman talks us through his work on evolutionary game theory, and the radical argument that our perceptions do not coincide with reality.
speaker_desc: Donald Hoffman, author of The case Against Reality: How Evolution Hid the Truth from Our Eye, is a cognitive psychologist and professor in the Department of Cognitive Sciences at the University of California, with joint appointments in the Department of Philosophy, the Department of Logic and Philosophy of Science, and the School of Computer Science.
subtitle: On Reality and Perception

title: Catherine Heymans | In-depth Interview
description: Astrophysicist Catherine Heymans discusses dark energy, dark matter, and the keys to uncovering the mysteries of the dark universe.
speaker_desc: Catherine Heymans is a British astrophysicist and Professor at the University of Edinburgh, based at the Royal Observatory.
subtitle: On dark energy, dark matter and beyond

title: Roger Penrose | In-depth Interview
description: Roger Penrose on the origins of the universe, opposition to Big Bang theory, and the implications of quantum mechanics, touching on Hawking Points & Twistor Theory.
speaker_desc: Roger Penrose is a mathematical physicist best known for his work on general relativity. He shared the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for their work on black holes.
subtitle: On Gravity and Quantum Mechanics

title: John Ellis | In-depth interview
description: CERN physicist John Ellis discusses supersymmetry, string theory and whether there could be a theory of everything that helps us understand the dark universe.
speaker_desc: CERN physicist John Ellis is a pioneer in the emerging field of particle astrophysics, who has also made important contributions to particle physics, astrophysics, cosmology and quantum gravity.
subtitle: On Supersymmetry, Dark Matter, and beyond

title: David Blunkett | In-depth interview
description: Former Home Secretary and Labour party MP David Blunkett discusses Brexit, the Irish backstop, UK immigration policy, and Tony Blair's legacy from Iraq to privatisation.
speaker_desc: Blind since birth, and coming from one of Sheffield's most deprived districts, David Blunkett rose to become Education and Employment Secretary, Home Secretary, and Work and Pensions Secretary during Tony Blair's years in office.
subtitle: On Tony Blair, Brexit, and Windrush

title: Anna Soubry | In-depth Interview
description: Change UK leader Anna Soubry on populism, the rise of the right, and how to fix the UK’s broken politics.
speaker_desc: Anna Soubry is MP for Broxtowe and a member of the Independent Group. Having threatened repeatedly to leave the Conservative Party on account of its leadership's Brexit stance, Soubry defected to the newly-formed group in February 2019.
subtitle: On the spread of populism

title: The age of surveillance capitalism
description: Shoshana Zuboff lifts the lid on surveillance capitalism, the new economic logic invented by Google and weaponised by Cambridge Analytica.
speaker_desc: Shoshana Zuboff is Charles Edward Wilson Professor Emeritus at Harvard Business School and a leading theorist of technology and privacy.
subtitle: Why we all have something to hide

title: Modern Crises and Ancient Gods
description: Will science or spirituality provide solutions to the climate crisis? The Green Party’s Natalie Bennett debates with David King and Sister Jayanti.
speaker_desc: Recent leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett, former chief science adviser David King, and European director of Brahma Kumari Sister Jayanti discuss what we must learn from the ancients to save our planet from its modern crises. David Malone hosts.
subtitle: What can save us from the climate crisis?

title: The Mystery of Life
description: The search for extraterrestrial life goes on, but will we recognise what we find as life at all? Nick Lane, Monica Grady and Airbus' Ralph Cordey discuss the nature of life and Earth and beyond.
speaker_desc: Biochemist and author of The Vital Question Nick Lane, Head of Future Missions at Airbus Ralph Cordey, and leading British space scientist Monica Grady grapple with the mysterious puzzles of life. In partnership with Airbus.
subtitle: Would we recognise alien life as life at all?

title: On the Dogmatism Paradox
description: Saul Kripke considers whether we are ever justified in dogmatically refusing to consider evidence that contradicts our beliefs.
speaker_desc: Should one decide in advance never to consider evidence against what one knows? There is an argument that seems to show this. Saul Kripke explores the question of whether the dogmatic attitude is sometimes warranted.
subtitle: Is it always wrong to refuse evidence?

title: The end of Left and Right
description: Rory Stewart, David Goodhart, and Chantal Mouffe consider the future of Left and Right as events in UK politics blur the line between Conservative and Liberal
filename: HTLGI2019_L26_The End of Left and Right.HD_1.mp4
speaker_desc: Author of The Road to Somewhere David Goodhart, Conservative leadership candidate Rory Stewart and political theorist and author of For a Left Populism Chantal Mouffe debate new political divides.
subtitle: Blurring the line between Liberal and Conservative

title: The Arc of Life: Michael Morpurgo
description: Extended interview with Michael Morpurgo, author of War Horse, on how his biography and life experiences have shaped his ideas and works.
speaker_desc: In this biographical interview with critic and novelist Stephanie Merritt, Michael Morpurgo considers the role of children's fiction in cultivating empathy, and outlines how his latest book Boy Giant uses Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels as a springboard to discussing issues such as the refugee crisis, and Brexit.
subtitle: How reading cultivates empathy

title: A Mad World
description: Is this really a mad world? Is the rise in mental health problems down to modern living or are we medicalising normal huamn behaviour?
speaker_desc: Author of Madness Explained, Richard Bentall, clinical psychologist Lucy Johnstone, and consultant for Public Health Wales and Swansea Professor of Medicine Ann John examine the evidence.
subtitle: Is modern life bad for your mental health?

title: Into the Unknown
description: Is the future of space exploration commercial, robotic or manned, and will we go beyond our solar system? Martin Rees, Tony Milligan and Elizabeth Seward debate.
speaker_desc: Astronomer Royal Martin Rees, philosopher and author of Nobody Owns the Moon Tony Milligan, and Senior Strategist for Airbus Elizabeth Seward reach out to the cosmos. In partnership with Airbus.
subtitle: What is the future of space exploration?

title: How to be a Stoic
description: Hear philosopher of science and author of How to be a Stoic Massimo Pigliucci explain how stoicism can help us focus on what really matters, and confront the challenges of modern life.
speaker_desc: Massimo Pigliucci is Professor of Philosophy at CUNY-City College, formerly co-host of the Rationally Speaking Podcast, and formerly the editor in chief for the online magazine Scientia Salon .
subtitle: Live your Best Life

title: Reason, rage and revolution
description: Will tolerance and pluralism give way to populism and revolution in the UK and beyond? Aaron Bastani debates with the Lib Dem’s Vince Cable and Ella Whelan.
speaker_desc: Founder of Novara Media Aaron Bastani, former leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable, and political commentator and journalist Ella Whelan consider the conflict to come. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
subtitle: Have tolerance and pluralism run their course?

title: How to Rediscover Your Creativity
description: Lauren Baker provides a workshop to enhance your creative skills and blue sky thinking with easy visualisation exercises, designed to unlock artistic potential.
speaker_desc: Lauren Baker is a British contemporary artist, who has created installations at the V&A, Tate Britain, and Tate Modern. Her Damien Hirst-inspired workshop was the Tate Modern's most popular to date.
subtitle: Why blue sky thinking is essential

title: Britain in Uncharted Territory
description: Former Green party leader Natalie Bennett, Labour’s Owen Smith, MEP Claire Fox and the BBC’s Sean Curran debate Brexit and the changing landscape of UK politics.
speaker_desc: Former leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett, left-wing Leaver and Brexit party MEP Claire Fox, and Labour MP Owen Smith consider how we might navigate this uncertain future. BBC parliamentary correspondent Sean Curran hosts.
subtitle: The uncertain future of UK politics

title: Rory Stewart in conversation with Emma Barnett
description: Former Conservative MP turned Independent candidate for the Mayor of London Rory Stewart talks to Emma Barnett on Boris Johnson's abuses of power.
speaker_desc: Conservative party leadership candidate Rory Stewart was one of 21 anti no-deal rebels to be purged from the party on 3rd September 2019. The former Secretary of State for International Development under Theresa May is now an independent politician and champion of the fight against a No Deal Brexit. Rory Stewart is interviewed by the journalist Emma Barnett, who regularly presents BBC's Newsnight , Radio 5 Live , and Woman's Hour .
subtitle: Former Conservative speaks out on abuses of power

title: The Arc of Life: Roger Penrose
description: Eminent theoretical physicist and Stephen Hawking collaborator Roger Penrose discusses logic, quantum and consciousness in this interview with David Malone.
speaker_desc: Sir Roger Penrose is one of the world's most prominent theoretical physicists, who collaborated with Stephen Hawking to produce the mathematics that showed how stars collapse to form black holes. Penrose invented twistor theory, spin networks, and many other quantum mechanical concepts, earning him the title of the founding father of quantum gravity.
subtitle: Nobel Prize winning physicist on his life and work

title: The Prejudice of Facts
description: Are alternative facts and fake news a recent invention or was objective truth always a myth? Perhaps Nietzsche was right to say ‘no facts, only interpretations’.
speaker_desc: Clerk Maxwell professor of theoretical physics John Ellis, post-Kuhnian sociologist of scientific knowledge S. Barry Barnes, and novelist Joanna Kavenna debate whether alternative facts are further proof that there is no objective truth. Phillip Dodd chairs.
subtitle: Are there no facts, only interpretations?

title: Immigration and Identity
description: Labour MP Thangam Debbonaire investigates why immigration has come to define UK politics and divide the nation, in this rethink of borders, identity and Europe.
speaker_desc: Labour MP Thangam Debbonaire is shadow whip in Corbyn's front bench team. She describes herself as a democratic socialist and a supporter of "fettered capitalism".
subtitle: Britain, Brexit, and borders

title: The New Mafia
description: Big Tech exploit their monopoly to manipulate users, eliminate competition, and evade tax. Should we regulate or tax tech giants or is it already too late?
speaker_desc: Conservative MP and former Education Secretary Nicky Morgan joins economist and award-winning journalist Anatole Kaletsky and director of ResPublica think tank Phillip Blond to debate the threat of the digital giants. Stephanie Hare hosts.
subtitle: Is it too late to regulate tech giants?

title: The Ladder of Success
description: Labour MP Dawn Butler argues for transparency in the career ladder so that improved gender representation at senior level confers benefits for all working women.
speaker_desc: Labour MP Dawn Butler is the Shadow Women & Equalities Secretary, and former Shadow Minister for Diverse Communities.
subtitle: How empowerment can fight inequality

title: The lure of Lucifer
description: Terry Eagleton, Susan Neiman, and Stephen de Wijze consider the philosophy behind our fascination with evil and violence, from crime fiction to serial killers.
speaker_desc: One of Britain's most influential cultural critics Terry Eagleton, author of Evil in Modern Thought Susan Neiman, and philosopher Stephen de Wijze get to the bottom of evil's strange allure.
subtitle: Why do we love Evil?

title: Momentum and Young Socialists
description: Giles Fraser, Anglican priest, outspoken journalist and regular panelist on The Moral Maze, talks to Jon Lansman, the founder of Momentum - the pro-Corbyn, grassroots political movement that has polarised the Labour party since its inception. Hear Giles find out about Jon's life experiences and core values in an attempt to find out what "makes him tick".
subtitle: In conversation with Jon Lansman

title: The Right to be Offended
description:
Last year Ireland voted to get rid of its blasphemy laws, and most applauded the new right to offend the Catholic Church. We also expect our press and our comedians to be viciously critical of, even offensive to, our leaders. Yet to avoid giving offence, student campuses are introducing no-platforming and safe spaces. Should we seek to eradicate offence to create a more tolerant and equal society? Or is offence vital to freedom and a critical means of containing the powerful? Please be aware that, due to the nature of this debate, this video contains language that some viewers may find offensive.

David Aaronovitch is an award-winning journalist and broadcaster. Joanna Williams is the author of Women vs Feminism, associate editor of the political magazine Spiked, and the Head of Education and Culture at Policy Exchange. Yasmin Alibhai-Brown is a respected pundit who writes regularly for the I, International Business Times, and New European.
speaker_desc: David Aaronovitch is an award-winning journalist and broadcaster. Joanna Williams is the author of Women vs Feminism , associate editor of the political magazine Spiked , and the Head of Education and Culture at Policy Exchange. Yasmin Alibhai-Brown is a respected pundit who writes regularly for the I , International Business Times , and New European .
subtitle: Should we seek to eradicate offence?

title: Science and Religion
description:
Are religion and science necessarily in conflict? What are the limits of a rational world view? Alister McGrath was once an atheist and is now an Anglican priest, physicist and intellectual historian whose books include Dawkins' God. Hear him delve into the debate around science, religion, and their changing relationship.

Director of the Ian Ramsey Centre and Andreas Idreos Professor of Science and Relgion at Oxford, Alister McGrath is a theologian, priest and intellectual historian.
speaker_desc: Director of the Ian Ramsey Centre and Andreas Idreos Professor of Science and Relgion at Oxford, Alister McGrath is a theologian, priest and intellectual historian.
subtitle: Can science and religion coexist?

title: The End of All Things
description:
We tend to think of physical, material things as the ultimate stuff of the universe. Yet contemporary physics has largely abandoned physical things in favour of energy and fields. And the late Mary Midgley argued that materialism was a profound mistake. Should we give up on our conviction that physical stuff is the bedrock of the world, or is such talk ivory tower nonsense?

Head of Particle Theory at Oxford Professor Subir Sarkar, former mathematician turned philosopher of science Nancy Cartwright, and philosopher of science and author of The Disorder of Things John Dupré go in search of the stuff of the universe.
speaker_desc: Head of Particle Theory at Oxford Professor Subir Sarkar, former mathematician turned philosopher of science Nancy Cartwright , and philosopher of science and author of The Disorder of Things John Dupré go in search of the stuff of the universe.
subtitle: What is reality made of?

title: What's next for the Left?
description: Many think British politics is more divided and more uncertain than ever before. What's next for the Left? Angela Eagle, Labour MP and author of The New Serfdom, puts forward her vision for the future.
filename: HTLGI2019_287 THE FUTURE OF THE LEFT.hd.mp4
speaker_desc: Former Shadow Secretary of State for Business, Innovation and Skills and author of The New Serfdom.
subtitle: How to Defeat Conservative Ideas

title: Where Women Rule
description:
The Patriarchy has become a powerful feminist watchword for the unequal division of power between men and women. In some fields, though, the tables have turned, with women a third more likely to go to university, three quarters of teachers being women, and the courts predominantly giving women custody of children. Should we be demanding equality for men in these areas? Or are there arenas where equality is a mistaken goal and women should have the upper hand?

Director of the ResPublica think tank, Phillip Blond, author of Women vs. Feminism, 
 Joanna Williams, and Kurdish women's activist Elif Sarican, consider the complexities and perils of power.
speaker_desc: Director of the ResPublica think tank, Phillip Blond, author of Women vs. Feminism, Joanna Williams, and Kurdish women's activist Elif Sarican, consider the complexities and perils of power.
subtitle: The age of anti-patriarchy

title: How to Make the Right Decision
description:
Cognitive science has shown that all of us suffer from biases that distort our reality, impair our judgement and lead us to bad decisions. Hear author and head of philosophy at LSE, J. McKenzie Alexander guide a workshop session that talks through the findings of contemporary decision theory and what's really involved when we make a choice.

Head of Philosophy at the London School of Economics, Jason McKenzie Alexander is an expert in evolutionary game theory and its application to the evolution of morality and social norms.
filename: HTLGI2019_280_How to make the right decision.hd.mp4
speaker_desc: Head of Philosophy at the London School of Economics, Jason McKenzie Alexander is an expert in evolutionary game theory and its application to the evolution of morality and social norms.
subtitle: Fixing your biases with cognitive science

title: Mirror, Mirror
description: We think being authentic is about remaining true to who we are, and many of us consider plastic surgery as a the preserve of tabloid celebritis rather than people like us. But from Caitlin Jenner to Chelsea Manning, plastic surgery is now seen as a means to ensure our bodies reflect authentic inner lives. Should we embrace cosmetic transformation as a way of becoming closer to who we really are, or who we might wish to become? Or should we be seeking to end society's obsession with appearance? Plastic Surgeon Miles Berry, radical feminist activist Julia Long and LGBT Labour Trans Officer Heather Peto consider apperance and identity.
speaker_desc: Plastic surgeon Miles Berry, radical feminist activist Julia Long and LGBT Labour Trans Officer Heather Peto consider apperance and identity.
subtitle: Can plastic surgery make you more authentic?

title: Liz Truss on Britain's Future
description: What will the United Kingdom look like in the future? Which issues should dominate British politics after Brexit? New UK Prime Minister Liz Truss makes predictions and puts forward her vision for the UK. Liz Truss was Secretary of State for International Trade and President of the Board of Trade. In 2016, Liz Truss became the first ever female Lord Chancellor. She has served as Conservative MP for South West Norfolk since 2010.
speaker_desc: Liz Truss is the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the leader of the Conservative Party.
subtitle: Brexit and beyond

title: The Dark and the Digital
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/A1HDHTLGI2019_99_The Dark and the Digital_Full Debate_IAI TV.HD.mp4
description:
Most of us like to think that people are good, yet the anonymity of the internet has enabled an epidemic of abuse. Do we need the oversight of others to behave well? Was Hobbes right that humankind is at its core wicked and in need of constraint? Perhaps internet surveillance could create a better world, but is there an alternative where our essential goodness would flourish without us needing to be watched? 

Award-winning journalist and commentator Yasmin Alibhai-Brown debates with Nigel Inkster, former Director of Operations and Intelligence at MI6, Ella Whelan, political commentator and assistant editor at Spiked, and author and former UN macroeconomist Janne Teller.
filename: A1HDHTLGI2019_99_The Dark and the Digital_Full Debate_IAI TV.HD.mp4
speaker_desc: Award-winning journalist and commentator Yasmin Alibhai-Brown debates with Nigel Inkster, former Director of Operations and Intelligence at MI6, Ella Whelan, political commentator and co-convenor of the Battle of Ideas festival, and author and former UN macroeconomist Janne Teller.
subtitle: Cyberbullying, Trolling & Free Speech

title: The Mathematics of Thought
description:
What does mathematics have to do with the nature of human thought? How does it change how philosophers think of reality? Philosopher and author of 'Ineffability and its Metaphysics', Silvia Jonas explains how mathematics has come to shape our politics, ethics and our very idea of what the world is.

Minerva Fellow at the Munich Center for Mathematical Philosophy, Silvia Jonas is in the Fast Track Program for outstanding female scientists by the Robert Bosch Foundation.
speaker_desc: Minerva Fellow at the Munich Center for Mathematical Philosophy, Silvia Jonas is in the Fast Track Program for outstanding female scientists by the Robert Bosch Foundation.
subtitle: How has mathematics changed philosophy?

title: The reality illusion
description: "Seeing is believing". "Seeing is the truth". Yet cognitive scientists seem to have uncovered these views as incorrect. Evolution led us to perceive what is best for survival and it turns out this has little to do with what we call 'reality'. Is reality then a creative construct that helps us to live but doesn't reflect the world? Are physical objects a useful hallucination? Or is the very idea of reality perhaps a mistake, and neuroscientists have just got it wrong? Cognitive psychologist and author Donald Hoffman, professor of philosophy and expert on metaphysical relativism Maria Baghramian, and post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson embark on a radical rethink of reality.
speaker_desc: Cognitive psychologist and author Donald Hoffman, professor of philosophy and expert on metaphysical relativism Maria Baghramian, and post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson embark on a radical rethink of reality.
subtitle: Has perception evolved to trick us?

title: How does Uncertainty affect Business?
description: How might the current political uncertainty be affecting the economy in ways we cannot yet see? Is capitalism - felt by many to be failing - going to make it through the next few decades? Eminent economist and author of Capitalism 4.0, Anatole Kaletsky charts the road.
speaker_desc: Eminent economist and author of Capitalism 4.0 , Anatole Kaletsky charts the road.
subtitle: Project Fear vs Project Reality

title: The New Politics
description: "It's the economy, stupid" has been the political truth for decades. But the vote for Brexit and wide support for Corbyn suggest that many would sacrifice growth for social change. Has the economy become less important to us? Are we turning to broader, more socially radical political goals? Or is the weakness of the economy since 2008 the very reason for the shift away from the centre ground? Cabinet Minister and Chief Secretary to the Treasury Liz Truss, Labour MP for Leeds East Richard Burgon and former leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable contest the importance of growth and seek plausible alternative goals.
speaker_desc: Cabinet Minister and Chief Secretary to the Treasury Liz Truss, Labour MP for Leeds East Richard Burgon, and former leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable contest the importance of growth and seek plausible alternative goals.
subtitle: Is the market the most important thing?

title: The Next Universe | Roger Penrose
description: What came before the Big Bang? What happens when our universe ends? Eminent theoretical physicist and Hawking collaborator, Roger Penrose, has a radical theory which proposes that another universe will follow our own.
speaker_desc: Sir Roger Penrose is an English mathematical physicist, mathematician and philosopher of science
subtitle: What if the Big Bang wasn't the beginning?

title: Tribal Identity and Tribal Conflict
description: Identity politics has become ever more influential. While the left champions identities based on sexuality or race, the right reasserts the nation. Does our desire to belong to one tribe or another make conflict with others inevitable? Could we do away with tribal allegiances and see ourselves as part of the same human family? Or are group identities based on class, race, sexuality or nationality the only effective vehicles for political change?
speaker_desc: Political philosopher Phillip Blond, Labour MP Dawn Butler, and former Home Secretary David Blunkett seek answers to issues of identity and belonging in an increasingly divided society.
subtitle: Does our need for belonging create conflict?

title: Clear Bright Future
description: How do we preserve what makes us human in this age of uncertainty? Broadcaster and author of Post-Capitalism Paul Mason covers markets, alogrithms, neuroscience and protest to put forward his new case for optimism, and how we can all be much more than cogs in a machine.
subtitle: How to be more than just a consumer

title: Universes and fairy tales
description: Should we recognise ours as the only universe and give up on others as fantasy science? Or is slipping through a worm hole into another universe a credible reality rather than a Hollywood fairytale? Harvard String Theorist Cumrun Vafa, CERN physicist John Ellis and author of Worlds Without End Mary-Jane Rubenstein dispute the possibility of universes outside of our own.
speaker_desc: Harvard String Theorist Cumrun Vafa, CERN physicist John Ellis, and author of Worlds Without End Mary-Jane Rubenstein dispute the possibility of universes outside of our own.
subtitle: Is ours the only universe?

title: On language and logic
description: Saul Kripke and Timothy Williamson discuss why language has come to dominate their field, why logic matters, and the future of Anglo-American philosophy.
speaker_desc: Saul Kripke has been described by many as the world's most influential living analytic philosopher and in the top 10 of the last 200 years. Timothy Williamson is the Wykeham Professor of logic at Oxford University - an institution that has played a major role in the development of the analytic tradition in the last century.
subtitle: Why language dominates philosophy

title: A New Socialism
description: What does Stalinism have in common with 21st century democratic socialism? Are modern forms of socialism merely adapted versions of capitalism? How can the ideals of communism, socialism and Marxism be used in politics today to create a fairer society? Jon Lansman, founder of momentum debates with Labour party politician Angela Eagle and journalist David Aaronovitch.
speaker_desc: Jon Lansman is founder of the 40,000-strong pro-Corbyn pressure group Momentum. Angela Eagle is a British Labour Party politician who has served as Minister of State for Pensions and Ageing Society and Shadow Chief Secretary to the Treasury. David Aaronovitch is an award-winning journalist and broadcaster. He writes a regular column for The Times which he has called "my war against stupidity".
subtitle: Where will millenials take Marxism?

title: Taking Humour Seriously
description: Is humour an essential form of subversion or a distraction from real dissent? Eminent literary critic and author of Humour, Terry Eagleton explores psyche and society to shed light on wit, irony and laughter.
subtitle: Is humour an essential form of subversion?

title: Decolonising Philosophy
description: Many see the search for universal truths about the world as the noble aim of philosophy. Yet our universities largely dismiss non-Western philosophy, and critics argue that British students are taught a narrow analytic approach. Are great ideas independent of time, place and tradition? Do African conceptions of the self or Chinese Mohist logic offer equally valid insights? Do we need to wake up to Western prejudice, or is there only one right way to think?
speaker_desc: Timothy Williamson is Wykeham Professor of Logic at the University of Oxford and world renowned philosopher of language and logic. Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad is Distinguished Professor of Comparative Religion and Philosophy, a Fellow of the British Academy, and an expert in the history of Indian philosophy. Nivi Manchanda is a lecturer at the School of Politics and International Relations at Queen Mary University.
subtitle: Do we need to wake up to western prejudice?

title: The Arc of Life: David Blunkett
description: David Blunkett: Former Home Secretary, David Blunkett was one of the most respected members of Tony Blair's cabinet. On top of the Home Secretary position, Blunkett also served as Education and Employment Secretary and Work and Pensions Secretary. In 2015, he was awarded a peerage and became Baron Blunkett.
speaker_desc: David Blunkett : Former Home Secretary, David Blunkett was one of the most respected members of Tony Blair's cabinet. On top of the Home Secretary position, Blunkett also served as Education and Employment Secretary and Work and Pensions Secretary. In 2015, he was awarded a peerage and became Baron Blunkett.
subtitle: The politician on his life, the left, and Labour

title: The Will of the People
description: From Corbyn to Trump, populism has rejected established political elites. Some think a return to ideology and emotion is a dangerous backward step, others that this means the alternatives have failed. Is populism on both the left and the right something to be celebrated or feared? Can giving more power to the people bring about positive, lasting change? Or is the only safe way to make progress to give it all to those that know best?
speaker_desc: Jon Lansman is founder of the 40,000-strong pro-Corbyn pressure group Momentum . Lansman debates with former Conservative Party Leader and Brexiteer, Michael Howard, who supports the Eurosceptic pressure group, Leave Means Leave . Joining them is Anna Soubry, MP for Broxtowe and a member of the Independent Group . Having threatened repeatedly to leave the Conservative Party on account of its leadership's Brexit stance, Soubry defected to the newly-formed group in February 2019.
subtitle: Is populism to be celebrated or feared?

title: How To Spot Pseudoscience
description: From climate change and evolution, why are beliefs that run counter to the scientific establishment so prolific? Philosopher of science and author of Nonsense on Stilts, Massimo Pigliucci looks at what causes people to hold these beliefs and how to separate the facts from fiction.
speaker_desc: Professor of Philosophy at CUNY and founder of Rationally Speaking , Massimo Pigliucci's latest book is Answers for Aristotle . His recent work focuses on the boundaries between physics and metaphysics.
subtitle: Separating Fact From Fiction | Massimo Pigliucci

title: What is the Power of Art?
description: We think art opens minds . Yet from medieval cathedrals to today's oligarch collectors, art has always stuck close to wealth and power. Is art necessarily the plaything of the rich and privileged and, as John Berger argued, a means of cementing existing heirarchies? can we imagine a more diverse world where art is for all? Or are the rich the fallguys and art itself an empty bauble?
subtitle: The work of art in the age of mass consumption

title: The Great Economists
description: Economist and former BBC Chief Business correspondant Professor Linda Yueh looks at the thinking of the great economists who changed the world and asks how their ideas can help us tackle issues such as Brexit, globalisatio and Trumpism as discussed in The Great Economists: How Their Ideas Can Help Us Today
speaker_desc: Linda Yueh is an economist, broadcaster, and writer. She holds a number of positions, including Fellow in Economics at the University of Oxford and Adjunct Professor of Economics at London Business School, as well as presenting a number of programmes on the BBC.
subtitle: How Their Ideas Can Help Us Today | Linda Yueh

title: Has Brexit Broken British Politics?
description: The European Elections have cast Britain into uncharted territory. And not just in a short term sense but in the longer term shift we are facing in our political and cultural environment. This debate focuses on how we navigate that uncertain future. Former leader of Plaid Cymru Leanne Wood debates with Shadow Secretary of State for International Trade and International Climate Change, Barry Gardiner, Conservative Party politician Mark Francois, and economist and writer, Anatole Kaletsky.
speaker_desc: Former leader of Plaid Cymru Leanne Wood debates with Shadow Secretary of State for International Trade and International Climate Change, Barry Gardiner, Conservative Party politician Mark Francois, and economist and writer, Anatole Kaletsky.
subtitle: Britain in Uncharted Territory

title: Money For Nothing
description: Once dismissed as a utopian fantasy, universal income has now hit the mainstream as a way to tackle inequality. With new technologies, support from across the political spectrum, it's no surprise people have begun to take the idea seriously. In a combative head-to-head debate, author of Basic Income: And How We Can Make it Happen Guy Standing goes head to head with leading libertarian economist Deidre McCloskey.
speaker_desc: In a combative head-to-head debate, author of Basic Income: And How We Can Make it Happen Guy Standing goes head to head with leading libertarian economist Deidre McCloskey.
subtitle: Guy Standing vs Deirdre McCloskey on UBI

title: Good and evil around the globe
description: From remote groups in Papua New Guinea to Pentecostal Christians, what can values and desires around the world tell us about the nature of morality? Is morality relative? Cambridge anthropologist Joel Robbins tours the globe in search of the good.
speaker_desc: Cambridge anthropologist Joel Robbins tours the globe in search of the good.
subtitle: Is morality rooted in culture?

title: Minds, Matter and Mechanisms
description: Neuroscientists believe that our minds and conciousness are no more than matter and mechanism. But if they are right, is all meaning, purpose and feeling illusory? Must we accept that we are just machines? Or do the secrets of experience require an alternative account of who we are? Author of Aping Mankind Raymond Tallis, German philosopher and author of I am Not a Brain Markus Gabriel and neuroscientist Susana Martinez Conde seek answers to the mystery of consciousness.
speaker_desc: Author of Aping Mankind Raymond Tallis, German philosopher and author of I am Not a Brain Markus Gabriel, and neuroscientist and author of Champions of Illusion Susana Martinez Conde seek answers to the mystery of consciousness.
subtitle: Are humans more than machines?

title: The Mystery of the Good
description: What is good for one is not good for another – the suicide bomber and the pacifist have very different notions of the good. Does this mean that there is no ultimate meaning to good and evil? Is good only found in the practical outcome of one's actions? Fear of Knowledge Author Paul Boghossian, philosopher of action Naomi Goulder and Philosophy after Darwin author Michael Ruse put good on trial.
speaker_desc: In this online debate, Fear of Knowledge author Paul Boghossian, philosopher of action Naomi Goulder and Philosophy after Darwin author Michael Ruse put good on trial.
subtitle: Is morality relative or absolute?

title: Beyond Quantum
description: Nobel Prize-winner Gerard 't Hooft examines Quantum Theory and its claims that reality is fundamentally uncertain and unknowable.
speaker_desc: t'Hooft is the author of Time in Powers of Ten and In Search of the Ultimate Building Blocks.
subtitle: Is quantum physics wrong? | Gerard 't Hooft

title: Something and nothing
description: The fundamental problem of philosophy, argued Heidegger, is 'why is there something rather than nothing?' Some scientists claim nothing doesn't exist and even the deepest space is full of virtual particles. Have we misunderstood the very idea of nothing? Is this little more than a logical mistake? Templeton prize winning cosmologist George Ellis, metaphysician Amie Thomasson and author of The Science Delusion Rupert Sheldrake get to the bottom of nothingness.
speaker_desc: Templeton Prize winning cosmologist George Ellis, metaphysician Amie Thomasson and author of The Science Delusion Rupert Sheldrake get to the bottom of nothingness.
subtitle: Is there something rather than nothing?

title: Equal Is Unfair
description: Equality is a goal most of us now share. But what if fighting against income inequality is misguided and dangerous? Director of the Ayn Rand Institute Yaron Brook explores the dark side of equality.
speaker_desc: Director of the Ayn Rand Institute Yaron Brook explores the dark side of equality.
subtitle: Inequality is not the foe | Yaron Brook

title: After Post-Truth
description: In a post-truth world, tribal agreement seems to have replaced reason and evidence. But is a world where our truths are tribal sustainable? Don't we need a shared framework of thought to prevent fragmentation and confrontation? Can we rely on evidence and reason whilst abandoning absolute truth, or do we need reality after all? Philosopher and novelist Rebecca Goldstein, post-colonial theorist Homi Bhabha and post-postmodern metaphysician Hilary Lawson confront the future of the post-truth world.
subtitle: How do we navigate a world where truth is tribal?

title: Beyond Men and Women
description: From Facebook's customisable gender option to popstars in drag, the traditional categories of male and female are now being challenged in the mainstream. Would a genderless world eradicate inequality or instead embed stereotypes? Should we keep gender and fight prejudice, or would a world beyond gender be both fair and free? In this debate, radical feminist author Finn Mackay, Labour MP Angela Eagle and Professor of Continental Philosophy Patricia MacCormack examine the potential and pitfalls of a genderless world.
speaker_desc: In this debate, radical feminist author Finn Mackay, Labour MP Angela Eagle and Professor of Continental Philosophy Patricia MacCormack examine the potential and pitfalls of a genderless world.
subtitle: Should we fight prejudice or gender?

title: Revolution in Rojava
description: In the shadow of ISIS, the community of Rojava is a flourishing experiment in direct democracy, gender equality and concerns about the environment. Now it's under attack. Back from Syria, Kurdish rights activist Elif Sarican tells this hopeful story. Activist for the Kurdish women's movement, Sarican is the UK coordinator of the Kurdistan Students' Union.
speaker_desc: Activist for the Kurdish women's movement, Sarican is the UK coordinator of the Kurdistan Students' Union.
subtitle: An experiment in direct democracy  | Elif Sarican

title: Morality of the Tribe
description: We think everyone should be treated equally. Yet we also think we are right to care most about our family, our friends and our lovers, and 82% of charitable donations in the UK are given to the causes closest to home. Should we embrace this, or go down Peter Singer and Effective Altruism's movement route? In this debate, barrister and founder of Effective Giving UK Natalie Cargill, Oxford political theorist and author of 'On Nationality' David Miller and human rights activist Peter Tatchell examine the tribal nature of morality.
speaker_desc: In this debate, barrister and founder of Effective Giving UK Natalie Cargill, Oxford Political Theorist and author of 'On Nationality' David Miller and human rights activist Peter Tatchell examine the tribal nature of morality.
subtitle: Should and can we treat all people equally?

title: War and Peace
description: Many think Trump a buffoon and a threat to world peace. But with IS weakened, and signs of progress in North Korea, perhaps his supporters can point to some initial successes. Could a belligerent approach to foreign policy make for a safer world? In this debate, founder of the European Council on Foreign Relations Mark Leonard and British politician and broadcaster George Galloway take Trump to task.
speaker_desc: Mark Leonard, the director of the European Council on Foreign Relations, and British politician and broadcaster George Galloway take Trump to task.
subtitle: Has Trump made the world more dangerous?

title: Limits of language
description: We think that everything can be talked about. Yet, from metaphors to the mystical, there are many things we seem unable to directly express. Are the most important things in life beyond language? Or can we find the right words for everything? Eminent literary critic Stanley Fish, Wittgenstein expert Genia Schönbaumsfeld and post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson scrutinise the limits of language.
